title: Senior Account Executive – DACH
description:
Position Overview:

This is a remote-first role based anywhere in Germany, with occasional travel (roughly 10% of your time) for in-person customer or team moments — proximity to our HQ in Tutzing is a plus, not a requirement. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender identity.

You’ll join a 15-person DACH sales team managing a shared base of 2,000+ existing customers, while also building new business from scratch. We need someone equally comfortable opening a brand-new account and growing one we already have — commercially sharp, technically curious, and credible with both IT stakeholders and business buyers.


You’ll get to take ownership of:

  • New-business hunting: proactively sourcing and closing new-logo accounts across Germany, Austria and Switzerland — sourcing matters as much as closing here.
  • An existing account book: owning and growing a slice of our 2,000+ customer base in DACH, spotting expansion and renewal opportunities alongside your new-business work.
  • Technically credible selling: running discovery and value conversations on data integration, EDI and supply-chain workflows, engaging both IT stakeholders and business buyers like supply chain and logistics leaders.
  • Full sales-cycle ownership: qualification through close, with accountability for your own pipeline health, forecasting accuracy, and ACV.
  • Direct, no-partner-model selling: this territory is direct sales only — you own the relationship end to end, with no channel hand-offs.
  • Staying sharp with AI-assisted tooling: our sales workflow uses AI agents for company research and a lead-scoring system, so you spend your time on conversations that matter.


We’d love to meet someone with:

  • 5+ years of closing experience in B2B software sales, with a track record you can back up — we check references and verified numbers, not just a good story.
  • A genuine blend of hunting and farming: you’ve opened new accounts from scratch, and you’ve grown an existing book — not just one or the other.
  • Technical fluency: comfortable in front of IT managers, EDI owners and integration leads, and able to translate that into a business case for a non-technical buyer.
  • A platform or data-integration background is a strong plus over point-solution SaaS experience — the independent, use-case-driven selling here is a different motion.
  • Domain exposure to logistics, manufacturing or retail is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
  • German native or C1+ level, with fluent English (our internal working language; HQ in Germany).

If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply!

Lobster is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment where empathy and respect guide our interactions



You can look forward to:

  • A personal, 100% individual quota — no team target to hide behind, and no partner deals to lean on either.
  • A fast, low-politics culture that rewards performance quickly: a quarterly bonus plus a year-end accelerator.
  • Remote-first flexibility across Germany, with purposeful travel rather than a fixed office routine.
  • A genuinely technical product to sell — not another horizontal SaaS tool.
  • A personal learning and development budget
  • 30 vacation days per year
  • Up to 20 days of remote work per year from any EU country
  • Bike leasing through our partnership with JobRad
  • Team evenings every Thursday, with refreshments covered by the company

Wir sind ein wachsendes Netzwerk mit Praxen in München, Hamburg, Köln, Düsseldorf, Berlin, Frankfurt und Hannover – und es kommen laufend neue Standorte hinzu. Dein persönlicher Verantwortungsbereich

  • Unterstützung in der Diagnostik und Behandlung: Du unterstützt unsere Tierärztinnen und Tierärzte bei der Diagnostik und Behandlung der Patienten vor Ort
  • Betreuung der Tierhalter:innen: Du sorgst dafür, dass sich Tierhalter:innen und ihre Haustiere jederzeit rundum wohlfühlen und hilfst bei ersten Fragestellungen
  • Assistenz während Operationen: Du assistierst während Operationen und bereitest unsere tierischen Patienten professionell darauf vor

  • Du hast Spaß daran, neue Prozesse zu implementieren und weiter zu optimieren, um das Erlebnis der Kundinnen und Kunden in unserer Praxis und damit auch deinen Arbeitsalltag ansprechend zu gestalten und stetig zu verbessern
  • Du hast einen innovativen und offenen Blick, möchtest dazulernen und fühlst dich in der Kultur eines Start-ups wohl

title: (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte (w/m/d) bei Dezernat Zukunft – Institut für Makrofinanzen
description:
Wer wir sind und was wir suchen

Ob die Energiewende gelingt, entscheidet sich nicht allein an Technologien, sondern an Kosten, Märkten und politischen Weichenstellungen. Genau dazu arbeitet das Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft – und um unsere Arbeit weiter zu vertiefen, suchen wir Dich. 

Das Dezernat Zukunft ist ein überparteilicher Berliner Think Tank an der Schnittstelle von Politik, Verwaltung und Forschung. Rund 30 Personen verfolgen gemeinsam das Ziel, Geld-, Finanz- und Wirtschaftspolitik neu zu denken und verständlich zu vermitteln. Geleitet von den Werten Würde, Wohlstand, Demokratie und Nachhaltigkeit suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt – idealerweise ab dem 1. Januar – für unser Energy Lab eine Person als (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte. 

In dieser Position konzipierst Du Analysen und Studien zu Energiemärkten – insbesondere zum Strommarkt – und führst sie eigenständig durch. Dabei betrachtest Du Energiekosten, Investitionsbedarfe, Gesamtsystemkosten sowie die Wechselwirkungen politischer Instrumente mit diesen Größen. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Fragen, wie sich Energiepolitik mit Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Nachhaltigkeit und Bezahlbarkeit zusammendenken lässt, wie Energiekosten strategisch und gezielt gesenkt werden können, und wie das regulatorische Umfeld so ausgestaltet werden kann, dass es den Erfolg der „zweiten Hälfte der Energiewende“ und damit die Erreichung der Klimaneutralität ermöglicht.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du analysierst Energiemärkte und -preise, einschließlich Systemkosten, und koordinierst dazu Forschungsprojekte. Dabei betrachtest Du auch fiskalpolitische Auswirkungen sowie Wechselwirkungen mit dem Stromnetzausbau. 
  • Du entwickelst konkrete Politikvorschläge, Analysen und Positionen zu den oben genannten Themen, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Deinen Kolleg:innen im Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft sowie den weiteren Teams der Organisation. Außerdem organisierst Du Expert:innen-Gespräche und andere inhaltliche Veranstaltungen. 
  • Du interagierst aktiv mit Vertreter:innen von Parlamenten, Regierungen, Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und Medien. Unsere Arbeit funktioniert nur dann, wenn wir mit diesen Gruppen im Austausch stehen, zuhören und zusammenarbeiten.


Das bieten wir

  • Eine Vergütung in Anlehnung an den Tarifvertrag des öffentlichen Dienstes (TVöD): Eingruppierung in Entgeltgruppe E 13 – abhängig von Deiner Erfahrung – inkl. Jahressonderzahlung und 30 Urlaubstagen.
  • Aktive Unterstützung bei Deiner Weiterentwicklung – fachlich sowie in Bezug auf Kompetenzen, Netzwerke und Aufgaben. 
  • Einen Arbeitsplatz in Berlin-Mitte mit der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten und gemeinsam vereinbarten Kernzeiten.
  • Unbürokratische, verständnisvolle Regelungen bei kurzfristigen Care-Bedarfen; bezahlte Freistellung nach § 29 TVöD bei persönlichen Anlässen (z. B. kranke Kinder). 
  • Einen Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket oder JobRad. 
  • Und nicht zuletzt: Ein dynamisches,motiviertes Team, gemeinsame Events (z. B. Berg- oder Paddel-Ausflüge) und Arbeit, die zählt. 


Dein Profil

  • Du teilst unsere Werte und Ziele, begeisterst Dich für Energie- und Klimapolitik und brennst dafür, dass die Transformation gelingt. 
  • Du hast einen Master-Abschluss in einem relevanten Fachgebiet sowie mindestens zwei Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung. Du kennst Dich in Energiemärkten – insbesondere im Strommarkt – aus, verstehst politische Instrumente und erkennst, welche Zahlen für politische Entscheidungen und ökonomische Weichenstellungen wirklich zählen. 
  • Du konzipierst und erstellst eigene Analysen – quantitativ wie textlich – selbstständig und gründlich. Du hast bereits erfolgreich Forschungsprojekte umgesetzt und Ergebnisse sowie politische Handlungsempfehlungen prägnant kommuniziert. Du bist Dir bewusst, dass unsere Analysen und Vorschläge in der Öffentlichkeit intensiv geprüft werden, und arbeitest entsprechend gewissenhaft und bist bereit, als Eigentümer:in für Deine Projekte einzustehen.
  • Du kommunizierst sehr gut in deutscher und englischer Sprache und verfasst in beiden Sprachen anspruchsvolle, gut verständliche Texte.
  • Du hast fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in der praktischen Anwendung gängiger KI-Programme. 
  • Du willst den Dingen auf den Grund gehen und jeden Tag dazulernen. Noch wichtiger als mitgebrachtes Wissen ist für uns die Fähigkeit, es zu erweitern und Meinungen zu ändern. 
  • Du arbeitest gern im Team, hörst zu und unterstützt und förderst Deine Kolleg:innen.
Die perfekte Kandidat:in erfüllt nicht immer jede Anforderung. Wenn Du glaubst, dass Du zu uns passt – bewirb Dich gern trotzdem und sag uns, warum.


Beschäftigungsbeginn & Vertragsbedingungen

  • Beginn: Von uns aus so schnell wie möglich. Im Anschluss an das Bewerbungsverfahren rechnen wir mit einem Start im Januar 2027. Das genaue Startdatum ist verhandelbar. 
  • Umfang: 32–39 Stunden/Woche (flexibel je nach Deiner Verfügbarkeit). 
  • Befristung: zunächst 1 Jahr (Entfristung nach zwei Jahren angestrebt).


Bewerbungsverfahren

Bitte bewirb Dich online mit Lebenslauf und einem kurzen Anschreiben, das Deine Eignung entlang der oben genannten Kriterien zeigt. Bitte teile uns auch mit, wie Du auf die Stelle aufmerksam geworden bist und welche Wochenarbeitszeit Du bevorzugen würdest. 

Bewerbungsfrist: 08. November 2026

Das Bewerbungsverfahren besteht aus drei Runden: im ersten Schritt einem Assessment-Test, der aus einer schriftlichen Aufgabe besteht und ca. 1-2 Stunden Arbeitszeit beansprucht; anschließend ein längeres Gespräch bei uns vor Ort im Büro und einem abschließenden Gespräch mit unserem Head of Energy Lab – Janek Steitz.

Wir schätzen Vielfalt und möchten die Diversität unseres Teams fördern. Bewerbungen sind willkommen – unabhängig von Geschlecht, Nationalität, kultureller oder sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Alter sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität.

title: Manager Robotic Sales Engineering
description:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Manager Robotic Sales Engineering (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as leading provider of automation solutions.

Your mission

Robotic Sales Engineers (RSEs) are RobCo’s technical face to the customer. They qualify opportunities, run requirement workshops, check feasibility and drive each deal to a concept our Solutions Development team can build.

As Manager Robotic Sales Engineering, you lead a team of around six RSEs and report to the Head of Robotic Sales Engineering. You make sure every deal gets the right technical lead, every customer gets a consistent experience and every RSE on your team keeps getting better. You carry a quota together with Sales and are measured on whether your team hits it.

You are a player-coach. You lead the team, and you still go on-site for the deals that matter most. You work where modular robotics, software and AI come together, and you help scale how RobCo brings physical AI into real production.

What you will do

  • Lead and grow the team – Hire, onboard and coach your RSEs. Run regular 1:1s, give clear feedback, write performance reviews and build real career paths.

  • Deliver the quota – Own your team’s quota together with your Sales counterparts. Track pipeline and win rates, spot deals at risk early and put your team’s capacity where it moves the number.

  • Steer the deal portfolio – Match RSEs to Account Executives and deals, balance workload and set priorities together with Sales and Delivery, so no customer waits and no deal slips.

  • Raise the quality bar – Set the standard for discovery, requirement workshops, feasibility checks and handovers. Review the critical concepts before they go to the customer or to Solutions Development.

  • Be hands-on where it counts – Join strategic accounts and complex workshops yourself, and be the technical escalation point for customers and AEs.

  • Own the interfaces – Work closely with Sales leadership, Solutions Development and Product to keep handovers clean and expectations aligned.

  • Improve how we work – Shape the team’s processes, templates, tools and KPIs, and turn field insights into input for Product.

What you bring

  • 5+ years in technical pre-sales, application engineering or automation projects, including 2+ years leading a team

  • You’ve run requirement workshops, won deals yourself and worked against a quota, so you know what it takes to hit it

  • You still enjoy being in front of customers and are credible with an engineer on the shop floor and a plant manager deciding on the investment

  • You make people better: you coach, give direct feedback and know when to step in and when to let your team own it

  • You set clear priorities when everything feels urgent, and you can explain them to sales, engineering and management alike

  • You build structure that helps the team move faster, not process for its own sake

  • You speak German and English fluently

  • You are happy to travel, around 30% of the time

  • Experience in physical AI (AI-based perception, learning-based manipulation, autonomous robots) is a plus

  • Experience building or scaling a team in a fast-growing company is a plus

  • A background at a robot manufacturer or system integrator is a plus

Why join RobCo?

  • Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

  • Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

  • As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.

  • Work out across Germany in over 7,200 studios with our subsidized Wellpass membership.

  • Flexible working hours, a modern office, and—depending on the role—the option to work from home.

  • Regular team events—from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.

About RobCo

Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that adapts to your use case, improves over time, and requires zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. With $160M raised from investors including Lightspeed, Lingotto Innovation, and Sequoia, 200+ people globally, and 2.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our RobCo Bay Area Demo Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

title: Staff Frontend Engineer / Frontend Architect (m/f/d)
description:
Introduction

Teaser

Two products, two backends, one frontend vision: build the AI-first frontend platform and design system that lets our engineers, product managers and designers ship UI at speed. A senior hands-on role with architect-level influence, no people management, and our CPTO as your executive sponsor.

Role at a glance

  • Level: Staff/Principal-level individual contributor – technical leadership, no direct reports
  • Reporting line: VP Engineering. Executive sponsor: our CPTO
  • Products: FactFinder NG (React on a Java backend) and Infinity (React on a .NET/F# backend)
  • Stack you'll shape: React, TypeScript, Web Components, design tokens, Storybook, AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, MCP-based tooling)
  • Team: Product & Technology organization of around 25 people, led by our CPTO, working in a product trio model with product and design
  • Location: Berlin; Munich, Pforzheim or Stockholm possible – hybrid with 2–3 office days per week; occasional travel (<10%) for offsites and design-system workshops
  • Start: as soon as possible

About FactFinder

FactFinder is one of the leading product discovery platforms for European eCommerce. For more than 20 years we've applied AI and machine learning to product search, navigation, personalization and recommendations. Our Product Discovery Experience (PDX) spans two products: FactFinder NG, an exact and highly configurable search, and Infinity, a self-learning, behavioral discovery engine. More than 2,000 customers generate over €160 billion in annual GMV on our platform.

We're around 90 people with a new management team, a clear growth plan and reknown investors behind us. Right now we're rebuilding our product and tech organization around an AI-first way of working and agentic commerce – and this role sits at the center of it.

Why this role exists

Our two products run two React frontends with very different technical roots. We need a vision, an architect, and an owner — someone who will unify them into a single, efficient system, build the shared design system on top, and enable product managers and designers to prototype and ship production-grade UI themselves with AI tooling. Incrementally, without a big-bang rewrite, and while both products keep shipping.


Your mission

What you'll do

  • Define and drive the target frontend architecture across both React products – one consistent, efficient React-based system, migrated step by step
  • Build and own our shared design system: tokens, component library and Web Components for embeddable shop UI, tightly aligned with Product Design
  • Create an AI-first prototyping and contribution framework – design system, AI coding tools, guardrails, automated review and CI – so product managers and designers can prototype and contribute production-grade UI
  • Stay hands-on: write a significant share of the critical code, set standards, and pair with and level up our frontend engineers
  • Work with a clear operating split: after architecture-focused first stints, spend around 80% of your time hands-on coding and 20% on architecture, design-system leadership and enablement
What success looks like
  • After 90 days: frontend audit of both products done, target architecture and migration roadmap agreed, design-system tokens and core components live, and the first prototype built and shipped by a product manager or designer on the new framework
  • After 12 months: both products run on the shared design system, the frontend rework shows measurable efficiency gains, and product and design prototype independently as a routine – frontend is no longer the bottleneck


Your profile

Must-have

  • Expert-level React and TypeScript, proven in complex production SaaS frontends
  • A real AI-first engineering practice: you use AI coding tools and agents daily and have built workflows or frameworks that others use – not just "I use Copilot"
  • Design-system architecture: you've built or led a design system (tokens, component library, Storybook or similar) that was adopted across multiple teams or products
  • Web Components (Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, embedding in third-party environments) plus a frontend architecture track record: you've modernized or migrated a frontend stack at least once, ideally several times
  • 6+ years in frontend or software engineering, including 3+ years at Staff, Lead or Architect level – setting technical direction across teams, not just within your own
  • Hands-on today: you write production code yourself – this is not a concept-only architect position
  • Business-fluent English (C1); no formal degree required, your track record counts
Nice-to-have
  • Technical leadership without line management: you've led a SaaS frontend team through a major technology change
  • Meta-frameworks such as Next.js and/or Astro – and a clear view on when to use which
  • Design-to-code and prototyping tooling: Figma workflows, design-token pipelines, AI UI generation (v0, Claude Code, Cursor, MCP-based tooling)
  • eCommerce, search or product discovery frontends (search UIs, embeddable shop widgets)
  • React on non-JavaScript backends (Java/Spring, .NET); Fable/Feliz or Ant Design
  • Good German language skills


Bonus Points

Who thrives here

  • Builders who ship code themselves and lead by example
  • Pragmatic simplifiers: incremental migration over big-bang rewrites, no over-engineering
  • Change agents with strong opinions, weakly held – able to transform an organization without burning it out
  • Enablers who enjoy making product managers and designers productive and treat them as peers
Probably not for you if you'd rather produce architecture concepts than running code, want to go deep on one product and leave the cross-product system to others, or are looking for a people-management role.


THE JOY OF WORKING WITH US

What we offer

  • Real ownership with executive backing: you shape the frontend of two products end to end. You report to our VP Engineering; our CPTO is the executive sponsor of this role – both agree the target architecture and migration roadmap with you, and the CPTO reviews your 90-day goals and holds your final interview. A company-level priority, not a side project
  • AI-first as a leadership priority, with the tooling budget to match: Claude Code, Cursor or whatever makes you fastest
  • Impact without switching to management: a Staff/Principal IC track on our career ladder toward Principal/Distinguished – with the option to move into engineering management later if you want to
  • A product trio culture: engineering, product and design as co-owners, outcomes over outputs
  • Competitive compensation that reflects the Staff level of this role
  • Training and conference budget, 30 days of vacation, modern equipment, mobility offers and a company pension plan
  • Hybrid work with 2–3 office days per week in Berlin, Munich, Pforzheim or Stockholm

How we hire

Remote, with feedback within 48 hours after every step:

1. 30-minute intro call with our Recruiter Mirko
2. 60-minute technical interview with our VP Engineering (your future manager) and an engineering lead: one frontend modernization you led, your design-system story, and how you use AI day to day
3. Case study: a hands-on part (AI tools explicitly welcome – walk us through how you used them) and a 45-minute architecture session
4. Team panel and a 45-minute conversation with our CPTO – optionally on site

FAQ

Is this a people-management role? No. It's a senior individual-contributor role: you lead through architecture, standards and enablement, without direct reports.

Who will I report to? Our VP Engineering. The role is sponsored by our CPTO: the frontend platform is one of the CPTO's top priorities, you agree the target architecture and migration roadmap together, and the CPTO holds your final interview.

Which tech stack will I work with? React and TypeScript on both products. FactFinder NG runs on a Java backend, Infinity on .NET/F# (with Fable/Feliz on the frontend). Backend, F# and our search domain are things you can learn here – React expertise, Web Components, design-system architecture and AI-first practice are what you bring from day one.

Is "AI-first" real here, or a buzzword? It's driven by our CPTO and part of the career ladder for every engineer. Your mandate is to take it from individual productivity to organization-wide practice.

Two legacy frontends on Java and .NET – isn't that painful? That's exactly the mandate: unify them, and how is your call. Incremental, not big-bang.

Can I work fully remote? No – the role is hybrid with 2–3 office days per week at one of our offices.

Why eCommerce search? Because agentic commerce is where AI meets real purchase decisions – on our platform that's 2,000+ shops and €160+ billion in GMV a year.

Apply

Send us your CV or LinkedIn profile plus links to work you're proud of (GitHub, a design system, a talk, a blog post) – and tell us in three sentences how you use AI in your daily engineering work. No cover letter needed.

Your contact: Mirko Duus

title: Senior Product Manager, Wealth & AI (f/m/d)
description:
What we do

At getquin, we're on a mission to empower everyone to build wealth.

Founded in 2020, we started with a simple idea: help people see their entire financial life in one place, so they can make more informed decisions.

Today, getquin has grown into one of the largest wealth platforms globally, already helping over half a million users manage and grow their wealth. Our platform combines analytics, tools and community to make wealth-building accessible for everyone, not just the experts.

After launching in Germany, we've started expanding across Europe, with a focus on growing our user base, building valuable new features and helping even more people take control of their financial future.

If you're excited to help shape the future of personal wealth management, join us. We're just getting started.


What you'll be doing

You've built products for investors. You know what a TER actually does to a long-run return, why a user with four brokers has no visbility what they really own, and how differently people behave when the number on screen is their pension rather than their pocket money.

You've probably also hit the ceiling of what a chart can tell someone. Better tables, more filters, another allocation donut. The data was always there; the answer never quite arrived.

We have something nobody else has: a complete, cross-institution picture of a person's wealth. Investments, cash, liabilities and insurance contracts, in one place, for over half a million users. Your work is turning that into features and insights people understand and act on, and the interesting tools for doing that now include AI.

We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own that area. You'll work directly with the founders and the product team, alongside engineering and our financial advisory teams. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, and you'll mentor less experienced product managers on the team.

Own the wealth product area end to end

  • Set the product strategy and roadmap across the picture we give people of their wealth and how we help them optimize it
  • Decide what we build on aggregated portfolio data that nobody with a single-broker view could build at all
  • Own our efforts to stay on the forefront of digital wealth management services and play your part in disrupting a still very offline industry
  • Work the unglamorous, high-leverage problems too: data quality, coverage gaps, missing cost basis, duplicate holdings across connections, ETFs held through more than one broker. A portfolio insight is only as trustworthy as the numbers under it

Turn the data into something users act on

  • Define the insights we surface about someone's portfolio, cash position and risk, and why each one earns a place on their screen
  • Own our conversational AI assistant and our AI-driven insights: what they say, what they refuse to say, and how a user knows which is which
  • Set the quality bar for anything we tell a user about their money: accuracy targets, human review, guardrails, rollback. Decide when something is good enough to ship and hold that line when the pressure is to ship anyway

Own the numbers

  • Define the metrics for your area: activation, engagement, the insight-to-action funnel, and contribution to subscription conversion and retention
  • Run the experiments, including proper A/B testing, read them, and report what didn't work alongside what did
  • Live in your own product analytics and write your own queries and reporting, rather than wait for someone to give that to you


What we are looking for

You might be a fit if:

  • You've built wealth management, investing or portfolio products. You know the domain properly: instruments, ETFs, costs, allocation, risk, tax drag, and how retail investors actually behave rather than how they should. This is the requirement we're least flexible on
  • You've owned a product area end to end against a number you defined yourself, with real experimentation behind it
  • You've shipped at least one AI or LLM-based feature to production for real users, and you owned its output quality. 
  • You've shipped inside a legal or compliance constraint, and you can reason about where an insight becomes advice. 
  • Your product discovery produces evidence, not opinion. You can show us a real research artefact and a decision that changed because of it
  • You're fluent in English; German is a plus
  • You can work from our Berlin office, and you already have the right to work in Germany

That usually adds up to around five or more years in product, but we care about the evidence, not the year count. If you came to product from engineering, data science, research, design, financial services, or from a Product Owner role, that counts. 

Strong plus if you have:

  • PSD2, open banking or account aggregation experience
  • Insurance or brokerage product exposure, which matters as we move into advisory
  • Recommendation systems or personalisation at scale
  • Subscription and paywall experimentation
  • Experience mentoring or coaching other product managers
  • Your own portfolio, and opinions about it

If you meet most of this and not all of it, apply. We'd rather read your application than guess.

Work authorisation

This role requires an existing right to work in Germany. We're not able to sponsor visas or support relocation for this position, so we can only consider candidates who already hold German or EU work authorisation, or who can obtain it independently. We'd rather tell you now than after four conversations.

What the first six months look like

  • Month 1: you know the data model, the aggregation layer and its technology behind it. What our analytics do and don't cover, and understand how AI is already being used and where it. You've written down the three things you think are most wrong with the product today
  • Months 2 to 3: a written, agreed area strategy with a prioritised roadmap, a primary metric with a baseline, and, clear metrics that you will be monitoring and optimizing along the way
  • Months 3 to 4: the first thing you scoped is live to a user segment, with a read on the primary metric, and with quality measurement behind it if it involves generated output
  • Months 5 to 6: two or three shipped iterations with measured results, including the ones that didn't work, a quality bar the team applies without you in the room, and at least one junior product manager who's visibly better at their job because of you

You won't be measured on shipping volume. You'll be measured on whether your area got measurably more useful and more trustworthy.


Why join getquin?

Why join getquin?

We're a fast-growing B2C fintech, and here, your work has real impact. From day one, you'll take ownership of your domain, ship features end-to-end, and help shape the direction of a product used across Europe. We value initiative, ownership and creativity, not layers of process.

Three things that are specifically true of this role:

  • Wealth management is ripe for disruption. Following digitalisation waves of banking and brokerage services, we are leading those efforts across the next big topic for private individuals: better understand  and optimize your wealth
  • The data asset is genuinely rare. Aggregated cross-institution wealth for half a million people, with over +€25bn in connected assets. Trade Republic sees its own platform. N26 sees the current account. Nobody else in Europe sees the whole picture, which means there are product questions you can only answer here
  • You'll own the area, not a slice of it. At our size the decisions are yours

Ready to build something meaningful? Then join us at the forefront of making wealth building accessible to everyone.

How we hire

Five conversations, typically three to four weeks from first call to decision. We tell you where you stand after every step, and we respond within seven days at every stage.

  1. Recruiter screen, 30 min, video. Role, scope, the salary band, hybrid expectation, notice period, work authorisation. No trick questions
  2. Hiring manager, 60 min, video. Your product area ownership, the outcome you drove, and your depth in the wealth domain. This is the first real fit conversation, in both directions
  3. Product case, take home. We give you a real getquin problem on aggregated wealth data and work through it together. We know you already have a job, hence we do not impose an in-person case during working hours
  4. Cross-functional panel, 2 x 30 min, in our Berlin office. Cover in more depth your case study and deep dive further in your understanding of product metrics and approach to product development. Usually in person in our office.
  5. Close conversation, 30 min. Team fit, how you like to work, and whatever is still open, including your questions for a founder

Along the last part we will be making reference checks, but only with former employers. Once we have this, we will make you a formal offer. 

The whole loop runs in English. Tell us if you need any adjustment to the process, whether timing, format or accessibility, and we'll make it. You don't need to explain why.

  • Du kannst komplexe Probleme schnell erfassen, priorisieren und in konkrete nächste Schritte übersetzen.

🌏 Location: You can choose to work in a full-remote mode as long as you're living in either France, Italy, Germany, Serbia, or Spain.

Join us as a Senior Full-Stack Engineer in our Identity Verification team to turn our KYC flow into a service that works with any provider, and to help more customers get from KYC started to KYC submission. 60% of your time goes on the backend, with the web as your second surface.

You will report to Nicola, the Engineering Manager of the Identity Verification team.

➡️ What you’ll do

  • Make identity verification provider-agnostic: Replace today’s tightly coupled solution with one service that any team at Qonto can use, whichever provider runs the checks. This is mostly Ruby (90%), with some Go (10%)
  • Improve KYC conversion: Work across backend and web on the path from KYC started to KYC submission, our main objective for the team.
  • Own the web side of provider integrations: Load provider SDKs in the browser, handle the errors they return, and keep the web part running as usage scales. Expect roughly half your time on web at first, moving towards 30% as the work shifts to the backend.

➡️ What we’re looking for

  • Backend experience: You’ve built and run backend services in production, and you’re at ease being backend-first.
  • React on the web: You’ve shipped production web code with React, and you can handle maintenance and scaling work on an existing application.
  • Third-party integrations: You’ve integrated external providers or SDKs, and you know how to design so that a single provider doesn’t lock you in.
  • Range across the stack: You’ll own changes across backend and web, partnering with our staff web engineer on architecture and complex integrations.
  • Ruby, or the will to learn it: Ruby experience is a plus, not a requirement.

➡️ What we can offer you

  • Platform work with real users: You build infrastructure behind KYC, the first step every customer takes with Qonto, and you see its effect in the conversion numbers.
  • Build reliable verification flows: Handle provider failures and retries, improve observability, and help the team operate integrations safely in production.
  • A design problem with real trade-offs: We work with several verification providers, each with its own SDK, errors and behaviour. You’ll design the layer that makes them interchangeable, and untangle today’s tightly coupled solution so that changing a provider no longer touches every consumer.
  • A platform other teams build on: KYC is our first internal customer, with other teams potentially following, such as Security for password reset checks. You'll build reliable APIs that other Qonto teams can depend on, while making the verification journey smoother, clearer, and more reliable for our customers.
  • Support from day one: An onboarding buddy from week two, and a weekly one-to-one with your manager.

➡️ Your future manager

Your manager will be Nicola, our Engineering Manager.

  • His path? Nicola spent four years at Satispay, progressing from Backend Engineer to Engineering Lead, managing 6–8 engineers. He helped scale their SEPA payment infrastructure from a few thousand to over a million transactions per week before joining Qonto as an Engineering Manager.
  • What does he bring to the team? A people-first leadership style focused on helping engineers grow. He sets clear expectations, encourages autonomy and learning through experimentation, and values direct feedback and open discussions. His goal is to build confident, independent engineers who take ownership of their work.

title: Senior Backend Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.


Your Mission

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver.
You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath.
You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo.
Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties.

Tech stack: TypeScript (NestJS backend, React frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (multiple databases incl. PostGIS), queue-based job processing, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), IaC, Claude but all agents welcome


What you'll own

  • Build features across our Hasura GraphQL API, NestJS and Postgres. From schema design to resolver.
  • Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact.
  • Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am.
  • Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access.
  • Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable.
  • Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure.
  • Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job.


What success looks like

  • You have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use.
  • Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why.
  • You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it.
  • You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you.
  • You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how.


What it takes

  • You're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement.
  • You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast.
  • You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows.
  • You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy.
  • You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration.
  • You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem.
  • You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers.
  • You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them.
Bonus:

  • AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC.

  • LLMs in production, especially document or data extraction and making it reliable for actual user workflows.

  • Data pipeline work: staged, reproducible processing, dataset versioning.

  • Mentoring or leading engineers, or wanting to grow into it.

  • Debugging tooling and build issues, not just application code. Our toolchain moves fast and is occasionally non-standard.


Why Predium?

  • Stage: ~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Yes, it's messy sometimes - that's the whole point. If you're looking for a job with a finished playbook, this isn't the right fit.

  • Impact: You're not cog #100 in some company. What you build here runs in production and is what customers rely on every day. Your contribution shows up directly, in revenue and in the product.

  • Ownership: We don't manage your time, we measure your results. You get responsibility and freedom - and the expectation that you'll use both.

  • Compensation: Competitive salary, bonus, and equity. We want you to share in the success you help create.

  • Team: Office-first in Munich's Werksviertel, 4 days/week.

title: Senior Brand Marketing Manager (all genders)
description:
Über die Stelle

Pflege ist eines der größten gesellschaftlichen Probleme unserer Zeit. marta ist die führende Plattform, die den intransparenten Markt für 24-Stunden-Betreuung radikal verändert. Wir machen Pflege einfacher zugänglich, transparent und bezahlbar.

Wir haben viel ausprobiert und viel gelernt. Performance-Marketing läuft. TV haben wir zwei Jahre lang mit echtem Druck gefahren. Mailing, Print und Partnerschaften kennen wir aus eigener Erfahrung, nicht aus Fallstudien. Jetzt geht es um die zweite Stufe: aus einzelnen Kanälen ein System machen, das trägt, und aus marta eine Marke, die Familien kennen, bevor sie zum ersten Mal suchen.

Darauf arbeiten wir gemeinsam hin: die erste große Marke für Altenpflege in Europa. Die gibt es bisher nicht.

Wir suchen die Person, die das plant, koordiniert und schreibt. Du denkst dir Kampagnen aus und bringst sie bis zum fertigen Material. Du entscheidest mit, welchen Kanal wir als Nächstes aufmachen und in welcher Reihenfolge. Und du sprichst mit denen, die das möglich machen: Sendern, Veranstaltern, Partnern, Produktionen.

Wenn du es leid bist, deine beste Idee in einer Präsentation sterben zu sehen, ist das hier der Unterschied: keine Pitch-Runden, keine Freigabekette, keine dritte Feedbackschleife. Du stellst deine Idee dem Performance-Marketing und den Gründern vor, und ihr entscheidet im selben Gespräch. Was montags beschlossen wird, läuft spätestens in der Woche darauf.

Wir sind eine der größten Plattformen im deutschen 24-Stunden-Pflegemarkt, finanziert von führenden Investoren wie Capnamic, Almaz Capital, RTL Ventures und Swiss Health Ventures, mit einem bundesweiten Franchise-System und Teams in Berlin, Bonn, Sibiu und Danzig.

Level: Senior. Du planst und koordinierst: Kanäle, Budget, Timing, Briefings. Die Texte schreibst du selbst.

An deiner Seite: unser Senior Performance Marketing Manager. Dort liegen Analyse, Attribution und die Aussteuerung der bezahlten Kanäle. Bei dir liegen Marke, Kampagnen und die Kanäle daneben. Ihr arbeitet auf Augenhöhe an einem Funnel.

Founder-Nähe: du arbeitest eng und direkt mit den Gründern an Marke, Botschaft und Ideen. Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen.

Perspektive: Head of Brand mit eigenem Team. Die Bedingung dafür sagen wir dir offen: mindestens ein zusätzlicher skalierbarer Push-Kanal, der uns spürbar schneller wachsen lässt.

Start: so bald wie möglich


Deine Rolle in unserem Team

Du bist die erste Person bei marta, die ausschließlich für die Marke da ist. 8 von 10 unserer treuesten Familien würden marta weiterempfehlen. Diese Geschichte erzählt bisher niemand systematisch. Du gibst marta eine Stimme, ein Gesicht und Kampagnen, die hängen bleiben. Was du jetzt festlegst, ist das Fundament für alles, was danach kommt.

Was du machst

  • Kampagnen, die hängen bleiben. Du entwickelst Kampagnen für Familien, die vor einer der schwersten Entscheidungen ihres Lebens stehen. Keine Werbeanzeigen, sondern etwas, das man sich merkt. Und du bringst sie bis zum fertigen Material.
  • Kanäle planen und koordinieren. Du entscheidest mit, was wir als Nächstes testen, in welcher Reihenfolge und mit welchem Erfolgskriterium. Und du sagst genauso klar, was wir uns sparen, weil du Erfahrung mit verschiedenen Kanälen mitbringst.
  • Texte, die du selbst schreibst. Landingpages, SEO- und Ratgeber-Content, Anzeigentexte, E-Mails, Videoskripte, Social, Print. Am Anfang entstehen sie an deinem Schreibtisch, zunehmend KI-gestützt. Wenn ein Kanal skaliert und wir echtes Volumen brauchen, holen wir Unterstützung dazu. 
  • Produktion briefen. Für Film, Design und größere Produktionen arbeitest du mit Freelancern und Spezialisten. Du briefst sie, beurteilst, was zurückkommt, und hältst die Marke über alle Kanäle konsistent.
  • Social Media, UGC und Community. Hinter marta steht eine große Community aus Betreuungskräften. Daraus machst du Formate, Geschichten und nutzergenerierte Inhalte. Unser Ziel: der größte Pflegekanal Deutschlands. 
  • PR und Presse. Du arbeitest mit einer PR-Agentur, schreibst Pressemitteilungen und baust Regionalpresse als Kanal auf.
  • CRM und Lifecycle. Die Entscheidung für eine 24-Stunden-Betreuung zieht sich über Wochen. Willkommensstrecken, Reaktivierung, WhatsApp: die richtige Botschaft zum richtigen Zeitpunkt statt nur Bottom of Funnel. Die Strecken füllst du mit dem richtigen Content und hast ein Auge dafür was funktioniert und was nicht.
  • Botschaft und Tonalität. Du übersetzt unsere fünf Personas in konkrete Botschaften und Touchpoints. Familien entscheiden emotional und nach Qualität, nicht nach Preis. Dein Text muss das treffen.

Dazu kommen die Themen, die du als Erstes in die Hand nimmst: Bewertungen und Google Business Profile, eine Mechanik für Empfehlungen, Regionalpresse und die Sichtbarkeit von marta in der KI-Suche.


So sieht Erfolg aus
Nach 90 Tagen: die erste CRM-Strecke ist live, zwei Kanäle sind erfolgreich angetestet, die ersten Ergebnisse sind vielversprechend, und wir gehen in die Skalierung.
Nach 6 Monaten: die Markenbotschaft steht und ist an allen Kontaktpunkten sichtbar, zwei bis drei eigene Kampagnen sind live, und das Performance-Marketing arbeitet mit frischem Material statt mit denselben drei Anzeigen.
Nach 12 Monaten: marta hat eine Kampagne, die Familien wiedererkennen, der YouTube-Kanal wächst und liefert Material, das in anderen Kanälen weiterläuft, Branded und Direct Traffic steigen, und neue Quellen liefern verlässlich mehr als 3.000 zusätzliche Leads pro Monat..


Das bringst du zu uns mit

Auf diese fünf Punkte schauen wir. Alles danach ist ein Plus und kein Filter.

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre in Marke, Kampagnen oder Content. Agentur oder inhouse, beides passt. Die Jahre sind nicht das Kriterium, die Arbeiten sind es.
  • Arbeiten, die du selbst gemacht hast, nicht nur verantwortet: Texte, Kampagnen, Videos, Seiten. Zwei bis drei davon würden wir gern sehen.
  • Du schreibst sehr gut auf Deutsch (muttersprachliches Niveau, C2) und kannst eine Idee so aufschreiben, dass andere sie umsetzen können.
  • Du hast mindestens einen Kanal außerhalb von Paid Search aufgebaut oder getestet: Mailing, Print, Partnerschaften, Events, Podcast oder TV. Du legst Erfolgskriterien vorher fest und brichst auch mal ab.
  • Du hast mit externen Dienstleistern gearbeitet: auswählen, briefen, Budget führen, Qualität beurteilen.

Das hilft zusätzlich
  • Du hast selbst einmal einen Social-Media-Account aufgebaut und zum Laufen gebracht, beruflich oder privat.
  • Du hast eine Marke mitgestaltet und weißt, wie aus Farben, Designelementen und Sprache ein stimmiges Bild wird.
  • Erfahrung in CRM und Lifecycle (HubSpot, Klaviyo, Superchat oder Vergleichbares).
  • Video und Social sind dir nicht fremd. Du erkennst ein Format, das trägt, und bekommst es auch mit kleinen Mitteln umgesetzt.
  • Erfahrung mit KI-gestützter Content-Produktion und ein klares Urteil, wo sie trägt und wo nicht.
  • Erfahrung mit erklärungsbedürftigen, emotionalen Entscheidungen. Lead-Gen statt reinem E-Commerce.
  • Erfahrung im Verhandeln von Media-, Sponsoring- oder Produktionsbudgets.
  • Englisch C1 für die Zusammenarbeit im Team.
  • Wenn du bei ein oder zwei Punkten unsicher bist: bewirb dich und schreib uns, wie du dir das aneignen würdest. Wir entscheiden nach deinen Erfahrungen und unserem Gespräch, nicht nach einer Checkliste.
Diese Rolle passt nicht, wenn
  • du mit einem Rebranding anfangen willst. Logo und Farben sind nicht unser Engpass. Der Engpass sind Kampagnen und Kanäle.
  • du konzipieren, aber nicht schreiben willst. Am Anfang entstehen die Texte an deinem Schreibtisch.
  • du am liebsten in einer Disziplin bleibst. Dein Feld reicht von der Mailing-Strecke bis zum Gespräch mit einem Sender.
  • du Kreation nach Geschmack beurteilst statt nach Wirkung.
  • du lange Abstimmungsschleifen brauchst. Die Wege sind kurz, dafür entsteht viel in kurzer Zeit.


Warum marta?

  • Virtuelle Unternehmensanteile (VSOP nach Jahr 1) und Performance-Bonus
  • 27 Urlaubstage
  • 2 Tage Homeoffice pro Woche und Vertrauensarbeitszeit
  • Wellhub (Gympass): Zugang zu Fitness, Studios und Wellbeing
  • Ein internationales Team mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen in Berlin, Bonn, Sibiu und Danzig
  • Unser Prozess
  • Fachgespräch, kurze Kampagnenaufgabe, Kennenlernen mit den Gründern, Reference Calls. Wer im Prozess sitzt, sagen wir dir vorher. Entscheidung in der Regel innerhalb von zwei Wochen.

Deine Bewerbung
Schick uns zwei bis drei Projekte, auf die du stolz bist, und in zwei Sätzen, warum. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Schick alles an Wir stehen für Chancengleichheit und freuen uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Herkunft, Religion, Behinderung oder Lebensweg. Wir bauen bewusst ein Team, das die Familien widerspiegelt, für die wir da sind.

description:

Nopan is a payment performance platform built by former merchants, focused exclusively on account and wallet payment methods. We help large merchants, fintechs, and PSPs turn payments into measurable revenue drivers. We are payments nerds who are excited about global changes happening in the industry and we want and know how to make it better. In just 18 months, we secured our license from the Dutch Central Bank, formed partnerships with Europe's major payment schemes, including becoming a Principal Member of EPI/Wero, and went live with initial customers. Plus

title: Director, Experience Intelligence and Quality
description:
Our mission: eliminating every barrier to mental health.

Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.

Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. With outcomes independently validated by JAMA Network Open and the Validation Institute, Spring Health reaches more than 170 million people worldwide through leading employers, health plans, and partners.

As an AI-native company, we believe technology should expand the reach, quality, and humanity of care. Every Spring Health team member is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully, apply human judgment to AI outputs, and keep building AI fluency in ways that support their role and our mission.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Care Operations Intelligence, the Director, Experience Intelligence & Quality owns the voice-of-customer (VoC) signal infrastructure that captures what Spring Health’s members, providers, employers, and payers are experiencing. Additionally, this leader will own the standards our frontline support and clinical teams are measured against: QA methodology, rubrics, calibration, and improvement strategy across every channel. This role will be responsible for continuing to shift the VoC and quality teams into an AI native organization. This is a full time, fully-remote position, though the ability to be onsite in our NYC office once a week is preferred.

What you’ll do:

  • Build and run the voice-of-customer / signal-synthesis capability: consolidate unstructured member, provider, employer, and payer feedback into a single signal infrastructure. Insights Ops teams can act on directly go to QA, Training, and function owners; systemic issues needing product, policy, or process change get surfaced to Process Engineering, Product, and other cross-functional partners.

  • Own an AI-native cross-channel quality strategy: one measurement standard, one defect taxonomy, one sampling approach, and one calibration process spanning AI-handled and human-handled interactions.

  • Partner with Process Engineering on the diagnose/fix boundary: this role sets the QA rubric and methodology that AI-failure diagnoses are scored against; day-to-day gap-log triage sits with Process Engineering pending the working-session decision on scope.

  • Design a signal- and defect-prioritization framework so the highest-impact issues get worked first, partnering with frontline leadership to design and evaluate quality improvement initiatives (e.g., training updates, workflow changes, automation opportunities).

  • Own the tool stack used across VoC and QA, including consolidating vendors where possible.

  • Build out and manage a high-leverage team spanning all elements of the quality and VoC cycle: VoC analysts, quality strategists, and QA reviewers led by a Senior Manager.

What success looks like:

  • A working VoC signal pipeline — feedback synthesized, prioritized, and routed — with a measurable VoC-driven action rate and shrinking insight-to-action cycle time.

  • One quality measurement standard and defect taxonomy in place across AI and human channels, replacing two divergent stacks.

  • QA coverage of support and clinical interactions increasing via automation, with calibration variance and inter-rater agreement inside range.

  • Reliable critical-error (compliance/HIPAA) catch rates.

  • Leadership and cross-functional partners have a trusted, evidence-based read on where quality is breaking and why, across AI and human-delivered service alike.

  • CSAT trending up across member, provider, employer, and payer groups.

What you’ll bring:

Unser Serviceteam im Büro löst etwa neun von zehn Meldungen aus der Ferne und plant deine Woche. Du fährst zu den Kunden, bei denen wirklich jemand vorbeikommen muss. description:

You will join a highly focused team working at the intersection of large-scale generative modeling, distributed systems, and production engineering. Our mission is to develop and optimize video base models that power realistic, controllable, and emotionally expressive synthetic humans at scale.

This is not pure research. This is applied research with direct product impact.

You will work on advancing training recipes, scaling distributed systems, improving evaluation frameworks, and optimizing inference to ensure our models are high quality, stable, and efficient enough for real-world deployment. Your work will directly influence models used by tens of thousands of businesses worldwide.

You will own and execute end-to-end research and engineering projects, from hypothesis to production impact. This includes:

  • Developing and scaling latent video diffusion models tailored for human-centric video generation

  • Designing conditioning mechanisms to improve control (pose, emotion, script, camera) without sacrificing fidelity

  • Advancing distributed training strategies (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, sequence parallelism) under real compute constraints

  • Improving training stability at multi-node scale

  • Designing rigorous evaluation frameworks combining automated metrics and structured human evaluation

  • Optimizing inference for low latency, high resolution, and cost efficiency

  • Running controlled ablations and experiments to drive high-signal modeling decisions

  • Contributing to high engineering standards: reproducibility, experiment tracking, CI/CD, monitoring

You will be expected to move fast, run multiple hypotheses in parallel, identify signal early, and focus on outcomes rather than exploration for its own sake.

What we’re looking for


Must-have

  • Strong experience training deep learning models at scale

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills

  • Hands-on experience with diffusion models (image domain required; video preferred)

  • Experience with large scale multi-GPU / multi-node training

  • Good understanding of distributed training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed or similar)

  • Ability to design controlled experiments and interpret noisy results

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with video diffusion models

  • Experience in avatar or human-centric generation

Experience optimizing inference systems for production

Our stack

  • Python, PyTorch, CUDA

  • DeepSpeed, distributed training & inference

  • Sequence parallelism

  • AWS, SLURM, Docker

  • GitHub, CI/CD pipelines

Who you are

  • You are research-driven but outcome-focused

  • You care about shipping, not just publishing

  • You can explore multiple ideas quickly and drop low-signal directions early

  • You communicate clearly and present results scientifically

  • You operate independently but collaborate actively across teams

Why join us?

  • Build production-scale video foundation models in a fast-growing Generative AI company

  • Work on human-centric video generation with real-world impact

  • Tackle hard problems in scaling, stability, and controllability

  • Influence the direction of next-generation synthetic human technology

  • Join a highly technical, high-ownership environment where your work ships

title: AI Support Engineer Lead
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

 

At Dust, we're building for a new kind of AI Operator: people who rethink and rebuild how their teams work around AI. Not “how can AI help us do this faster?” but “if AI existed from day one, would we even do this the same way?”

 

As our AI Support Engineering Lead, you'll own how Support is built and scaled at Dust. This is a deeply hands-on role. You'll take on the hardest customer issues when our agents fall short, but your job isn't simply to resolve them. You'll look for the pattern behind each issue and turn what you learn into better agents, automation, tooling, documentation, and product improvements. Over time, you'll help grow the team and shape how Support Engineering operates as Dust scales.

 

You'll define, ship, and continuously iterate on the systems that make this possible: AI agents, automation workflows, classification systems, knowledge systems, and tooling built on top of Dust itself. You'll dogfood the product harder than almost anyone at the company and set the standard for how the rest of the Support Engineering team does the same.

 

We're looking for someone who wants to lead from the work: technically strong, obsessed with building better systems, and excited to shape both the team and the function as we grow.

 

What you'll do

 

Build the AI systems that do the work

  • Set the technical direction for the support stack: what gets automated, in what order, and to what standard. You make the calls, not just the builds.

  • Design, ship, and maintain AI agents and automation workflows that reduce manual support load: think ticket classification, acknowledgment automation, response drafting, incident detection, and proactive user outreach.

  • Identify recurring categories of issues and engineer them out of existence through automation, documentation, prompt iteration, or product feedback.

  • Build and maintain tooling (MCP integrations, Dust agents, internal scripts) that increase the team's capacity without increasing headcount.

  • Define and own the "Support as a Product" backlog. You decide what goes on it, coach the team to execute it, and hold the bar on what shipped means.

 

Run support when the systems fall short

  • Hire, onboard, and develop the support engineers around you. You're not just resolving tickets and building systems, you're growing the people who will.

  • Set the standard for how complex issues get handled at Dust. You take the hardest tickets yourself. The team knows what good looks like because they've watched you do it.

  • Investigate complex issues across logs, code, and internal tooling to identify root causes and provide clear answers to customers.

  • Handle escalated cases with precise, accessible communication for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Systematically analyze agent-generated responses for inconsistencies and iterate on prompts, documentation, and tooling until human intervention is minimal.

 

Bridge customer pain to product improvements

  • Represent support at the engineering and product level. You synthesize signal, prioritize it, and push it through with enough context that it actually moves things, not just relays it.

  • Build strong working relationships with engineers and customer-facing teams to ensure efficient, high-context escalations.

  • Own the feedback loop end-to-end: when agents fail due to missing or incorrect information, close the gap across engineering, product, and documentation.

 

Requirements

Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions: Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.

 

Aptitude

  • Function-building experience: You've defined or significantly shaped a support engineering function before: built the operating model, set the standards, hired into the team, or rebuilt a broken process from scratch.

  • High technical aptitude: comfortable reading code, analyzing logs, navigating codebases, and troubleshooting distributed systems. You're not stopped by a stack trace.

  • AI fluency at builder level: track record of building custom agents, automations, or workflows using AI tools (Dust, Cursor, Claude Code, n8n, etc.); not just prompting.

  • Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, what to escalate, and, critically, what to delegate and to whom. You make these calls for yourself and for the team, fast and without second-guessing.

  • People leadership: You've coached and developed engineers and know how to set expectations, give direct feedback, and raise the performance of the people around you.

  • Bidirectional communication: can translate technical concepts to non-technical audiences and speak technical language fluently with engineers.

  • Build/Run mindset: You believe the best Support Engineering teams don't just resolve issues. They build systems that prevent those issues from recurring.

 

Attitude

  • Builder mentality: You instinctively automate repetitive work rather than accepting inefficient systems, and you hold your team to the same standard.

  • Resilience-empathy paradox: You can absorb customer frustration without taking it personally while still deeply caring about the user experience.

  • Leads by example: You're not above the queue. When something is hard, you take it.

  • Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, and what to escalate.

  • Thrives in ambiguity: You enjoy building systems from scratch in environments where many processes are still undefined.

  • Low ego, team player: You share knowledge freely and care about the success of the broader team.

 

Agency

  • High ownership: You define what needs to be done as often as you execute it. You don't wait for someone to tell you the function has a gap.

  • Systems-first thinking: You focus on eliminating categories of work, not simply resolving tickets faster. You hold yourself and the team accountable to that distinction.

  • Pattern recognition to repeatability: You turn recurring issues into scalable systems, automations, workflows, or documentation that eliminate future occurrences.

  • Deep investigation instincts: You investigate as far as possible before escalating, providing engineering teams with thoughtful, high-context information when collaboration is needed, and you coach the team to do the same.

 

Even if you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We care deeply about curiosity, potential, and determination, and we know exceptional people don’t always fit neatly into a checklist.

 

Benefits & Compensation

  • Competitive compensation based on level and experience

    • 100,000€ - 160,000€

  • Significant equity package at a Sequoia-backed startup

  • Health benefits for you and your dependents

  • New MacBook Pro or Linux machine, monitor, keyboard, etc.

  • Opportunity to travel between our Paris and San Francisco offices

  • Regular team events and off-sites

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Head of ClinOps Data Management RWD/RWE
description:
À propos de Lifen

Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales peuvent transformer le système de santé, à condition qu’elles soient accessibles. Mieux les faire circuler, c’est réduire la charge administrative, mieux coordonner les soins et accélérer la recherche clinique.

Depuis 2015, nous développons des solutions qui aident les professionnels de santé à partager les informations médicales et les chercheurs à exploiter des données de santé. Plus de 150 personnes travaillent chez Lifen, depuis nos bureaux et à distance. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé en France.

Notre équipe

L’équipe Clinical Ops intervient au cœur de nos projets de recherche clinique fondés sur des données de santé. Elle transforme des documents médicaux en données structurées, nécessaires à la constitution de cohortes patients et à la préparation des exports utilisés dans nos projets de recherche.

Aujourd’hui, l’équipe structure environ 100 à 200 cas patients par semaine. Notre ambition : tripler cette capacité dans les 9 prochains mois, tout en maintenant un haut niveau de qualité des données.

Pour y parvenir, nous cherchons une personne capable de reprendre le management de l’équipe, mais surtout de piloter le flux de production, d’anticiper la charge et de porter une démarche d’amélioration continue avec les équipes Produit, IA et Engineering.

C’est un rôle à la croisée du management opérationnel, de la RWD et de l’amélioration de processus.

Ce que tu feras chez nous

Ta première mission sera de reprendre le pilotage de la production des cohortes afin d’en améliorer simultanément la qualité, la capacité de traitement et le niveau d’automatisation.

Concrètement, tu seras amené·e à :

  • Manager et faire grandir l’équipe Clinical Ops, en donnant un cadre clair aux priorités et en organisant l’activité quotidienne.

  • Anticiper la charge et piloter la capacité de production afin de limiter les bottlenecks et de mieux absorber les variations de volume.

  • Construire les outils de pilotage nécessaires pour avoir une vision fine du flux : volumes de patients, capacité de traitement, taux d’erreur, points de blocage et charge de l’équipe.

  • Construire et orchestrer une roadmap d’amélioration continue permettant progressivement d’augmenter la capacité de traitement.

  • Porter cette roadmap auprès des équipes Produit, IA et Engineering : rendre les besoins opérationnels visibles, suivre les livrables R&D et créer le rythme nécessaire pour que les améliorations soient effectivement délivrées.

  • Garantir la qualité des cohortes et contribuer à la préparation des exports de données nécessaires aux projets de recherche.

Ce que nous attendrons de toi

Dans les premiers mois, nous attendrons de toi que tu développes une compréhension très fine du flux Clinical Ops : où se trouvent les blocages, comment évolue la charge et quels leviers permettent réellement d'améliorer la production.

Ton succès se mesurera notamment à ta capacité à mettre en place un pilotage fiable de l’activité, à réduire les erreurs et les bottlenecks et à créer, avec les équipes Produit et R&D, un rythme d’amélioration continue suffisamment soutenu pour accompagner notre changement d’échelle.

À horizon 9 mois, l’objectif est clair : passer d’environ 100–200 à 300–600 cas patients structurés par semaine, sans multiplier les ressources par trois.

Ce que nous recherchons

Must-have

Nous chercherons en priorité trois éléments dans ton parcours :

  • Une expérience réussie en startup ou scale-up, dans un environnement où les process, outils et responsabilités restaient à construire.

  • Une expérience concrète de la Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence, idéalement autour de la constitution ou de l'exploitation de cohortes patients.

  • Un background santé ou scientifique te permettant de comprendre les enjeux liés aux données médicales et à la recherche clinique.

Nous attendons également :

  • Une expérience confirmée de management d’équipe opérationnelle.

  • Une expérience de structuration et de pilotage d’une activité complexe à partir de données et de KPI.

  • Une capacité à passer d’un problème opérationnel très concret à un plan d’amélioration structuré.

  • Une expérience de collaboration étroite avec des équipes Produit, Data/IA ou Engineering.

  • Une capacité à faire avancer une roadmap transverse et à créer de l’accountability autour des livrables.

Nice-to-have

  • Un parcours en data management, biostatistiques, épidémiologie ou dans un domaine scientifique proche.

  • Une expérience de structuration de registres, bases de données de santé ou cohortes RWD.

  • Une familiarité avec les enjeux de recherche clinique et les interactions avec les autorités de santé.

  • Une bonne compréhension des usages de l’IA et de l’ingénierie appliqués aux données de santé.

Ta manière de travailler

Tu as une vraie “just do it mentality” : face à un problème imparfaitement cadré, tu commences par comprendre les faits, tu structures le problème et tu mets rapidement en place les premières solutions.

Tu es particulièrement à l’aise dans les environnements où il faut créer les outils plutôt que simplement les utiliser. Si le dashboard dont tu as besoin pour piloter ton équipe n’existe pas, tu es capable de le définir et de le mettre en place.

Tu es structuré·e et organisé·e, mais pas bureaucratique. Tu sais entrer suffisamment dans le détail du flux pour comprendre les problèmes réels, tout en gardant une vision d’ensemble et en priorisant ce qui aura le plus d’impact.

Enfin, tu sais faire avancer des équipes sur lesquelles tu n’as pas nécessairement d’autorité hiérarchique. Tu rends les problèmes visibles, explicites les priorités et crées le rythme nécessaire pour transformer les décisions en améliorations concrètes.

Nos valeurs

Embrace Complexity — Tu aimes comprendre un flux de données complexe, en identifier les points de rupture et transformer cette complexité en décisions concrètes.

Bienveillance — Tu accompagnes une équipe au quotidien avec exigence, écoute et clarté.

Real Impact — Tu améliores la qualité et la disponibilité des données qui permettent de faire avancer des projets de recherche clinique.

Process de recrutement

Échange de préqualification avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager, 30 minutes. Nous faisons connaissance, revenons sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les grandes lignes du poste. C’est aussi le moment de répondre à tes premières questions sur Lifen, l’équipe et le contexte.

Entretien avec le VP Reasearch, 60 minutes. Nous revenons plus en détail sur ton parcours, ton expérience en RWD et en constitution de cohortes, ainsi que sur ton expérience de management et de pilotage d’activités opérationnelles. L’objectif est aussi de comprendre la manière dont tu structures et fais évoluer une organisation dans un environnement en croissance.

Use Case avec des membres des équipes Clinical Ops et Produit, 60 minutes. À partir de situations concrètes, nous échangeons sur ta manière de structurer une cohorte RWD, d’analyser des problématiques opérationnelles et de construire des plans d’amélioration. Ce sera également l’occasion d’aborder la manière dont tu gères les enjeux humains et la collaboration avec des équipes transverses.

Cultural alignment avec deux membres de Lifen, 45 minutes en visio. Ce temps permettra d’échanger sur ta façon de travailler, ton niveau d’autonomie, la collaboration au quotidien et l’adéquation avec nos valeurs.

Compensation: €65K – €75K
