  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

🤹 Operations at Alan

Behind Alan's performance lies an Operations team that is anything but back-office. At Alan, Ops is a strategic function: we define the vision, build the systems, and own the outcomes that make our insurance and healthcare products work at scale.

As a Senior Ops & Product Builder, you will own some of the most critical and ambiguous challenges in the company. You will shape strategy, drive cross-functional alignment, and build solutions with lasting impact on Alan's P&L and member experience.

You’ll be joining 80+ talented, committed, passionate Ops team members working globally on all our services. You’ll be among the team mates structuring this community.

⭐️ The challenges

We are looking for driven professionals and entrepreneurs with a strong operational background to disrupt the way we traditionally think about insurance or healthcare. Our goal is to delight our members everywhere as we keep on scaling and building new services in France and internationally.

The job description is simple: you set the vision, make the hard calls, and own the outcome.

Here are some examples of missions our team is covering that you could lead:

  • Saving millions through fraud detection: Building a detection capability with no playbook. Owning make-vs-buy decisions on tooling, balancing precision against member experience at scale, and managing the external surface. title: Full time paid Internship DSU/ Stage DSU Paris
description:
Introduction

The selected person will join the Technopolis Group Data Science Unit (DSU), whose members work across different country offices. Our growing team brings together diverse academic backgrounds and a shared passion for developing data science applications to improve policymaking.
The DSU contributes to policy consulting projects and conducts R&D to develop and test new applications, sometimes in collaboration with internal and external partners. Its work includes record linkage, classification, natural language processing, web scraping, generative AI and dynamic visualisations.
As an intern, you will work alongside experienced data scientists and policy consultants, applying and developing your technical skills to address real-world policy questions.


About this job

The role of the intern in data science for public policy will be to support the data science components of policy evaluations, sectoral studies and strategic consultancy projects. Our clients include French regional councils, the French Development Agency (AFD), ADEME, the European Commission and multilateral development banks.
You will be part of the DSU and collaborate with colleagues across policy areas, including science, technology and innovation, economic development, the green transition, international cooperation and health. You may also contribute to internal R&D and business development activities, particularly the preparation of data science approaches for project proposals.
No previous professional experience is required. Relevant coursework, academic research and personal coding projects will be considered.
We are looking to recruit a full-time intern for at least 6 months starting in Automn 2026. Internship should be sponsored by the intern’s university (stage conventionné).


Your profile

We are looking for a curious and motivated individual who enjoys working with data and wants to understand how data science can inform public policy.
Suitable candidates should have:

  • Master’s-level studies in data science, computer science, statistics, economics, engineering or another relevant discipline with a strong quantitative component, and be eligible for a university-sponsored internship.
  • Practical programming skills in Python, demonstrated through coursework, research or personal projects, and the ability to write and understand their own analytical code.
  • Good foundations in statistics and quantitative analysis, together with an interest in economics and public policy and in interpreting analytical results in their policy context.
  • Basic familiarity with machine learning or natural language processing, and an interest in using generative AI and large language models programmatically through APIs for data processing, text analysis and knowledge extraction.
  • A careful and structured approach to working with data, including attention to data quality, validation, documentation and reproducibility.
  • An interest in public policy and in using data science to support evidence-based policymaking, particularly in areas such as science, technology and innovation, economic development, the green transition or health policy.
  • Fluency in French and English, good communication skills and an ability to work collaboratively in an international and multicultural environment. A third language would be an asset.


Your responsibilities

Working under the guidance of experienced colleagues, you will:

  • Support the design and implementation of data science analyses to answer policy questions, writing code in Python.
  • Collect, clean, link and validate data from multiple sources, including open datasets, databases and web-based sources.
  • Help develop and test analytical workflows, potentially involving machine learning, NLP and LLM APIs for classification, text analysis and knowledge extraction.
  • Contribute to indicators, scoreboards and visualisations, including dashboards where relevant, to make findings accessible to different audiences.
  • Interpret and communicate results, helping prepare reports, methodological documentation and presentations for clients.
  • Contribute to the DSU’s R&D and proposal preparation, for example by exploring new datasets, testing methods or developing small prototypes.


Our offer

We offer a paid internship in Paris, with hands-on experience at the intersection of data science and public policy. You will work with an international, multidisciplinary team, receive guidance from experienced colleagues and contribute to both client projects and the development of new analytical applications.
Many of our interns become full-time staff at Technopolis or go on to pursue opportunities in the public and private sectors.

title: Communications Lead
description:
Who we are

Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.

We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.

Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role

Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth.

It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there.

You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day.

This is a freelance role on a 6-month contract, with a target start in Q4 2026.

Your responsibilites

Set up how PR works at Yubo

  • Build PR operations and onboard Yubo's PR agency, setting clear ways to spot stories, check facts, and turn insight into coverage.

  • Dig into Yubo's data to find trends and stories worth telling.

title: Infrastructure Engineer (ML Systems) - Paris
description:
You’ll own the GPU compute that powers our model training, evaluation and serving systems.

This role sits in our Infrastructure team, which works at the lowest layers of our stack, from Kubernetes down to the GPU hardware. You’ll run the clusters, GPUs and schedulers that our research, product and platform teams depend on, and manage the capacity we buy from our cloud providers.

What success looks like

Success is measured by how well we use our GPUs: keeping production reliable and improving the performance of our training and serving stack.

What you’ll be doing

  • Running Kubernetes clusters for GPU training and inference

  • Improving how GPU work is scheduled and placed

  • Detecting, draining and repairing unhealthy GPU nodes

  • Managing capacity with our cloud providers

  • Debugging failures in GPUs, Linux, storage and networking

The first year

By month 3, you’ll be handling a share of cluster incidents on your own and will have shipped one change to scheduling or node health, such as automatically detecting and draining unhealthy GPU nodes. By month 6, you’ll own one part of the compute layer outright: scheduling and placement, node health and repair, or capacity and new regions. By month 12, you’ll be responsible for a globally distributed GPU system that shifts capacity between training and inference as needs change.

Who you’ll work with

Your hiring manager is our VP of Engineering. Day to day, you’ll work with the Platform Infrastructure team, the research and product teams who use our compute, and our cloud providers and other vendors.

What we think it takes

You’re likely a good fit if you:

  • Have built and run GPU workloads on Kubernetes

  • Could design a GPU cluster for training and online RL from scratch

  • Debug confidently at the OS layer and below (Linux, GPU drivers, networking and storage)

  • Write strong Python

It’s a plus if you’ve worked as an SRE or infrastructure engineer, or have used:

  • Slurm

  • Kubernetes scheduling and autoscaling tools such as Kueue or Karpenter

  • Multi-cloud orchestration tools such as SkyPilot

  • AWS services such as EKS or SageMaker HyperPod

  • High-performance interconnects and collective communication libraries such as EFA, InfiniBand, NCCL or Open MPI

  • Terraform

You don’t need ML research experience. If you match most of this but not every point, please apply.

How we hire

Four stages, about three hours in total: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute coding interview, a 60-minute system design interview and a closing 30-minute conversation with our VP of Engineering. The coding and system design interviews are modelled on real-world problems you’d face in this role.

Practicalities

The role is hybrid, with three days a week in our Paris or London office and occasional travel between the two. We offer a competitive package.

title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions.

You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators.

This is a hands-on scientific leadership role. You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme.

You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions.

The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work.

What You'll Do

Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve.

Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality.

Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses.

Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims.

Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes.

Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations.

Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks.

Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications.

Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology.

  • Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings.

  • Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors, including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions.

  • A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health, with clear intellectual and analytical contributions.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures.

  • Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations.

  • Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English, including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning.

  • Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow.

  • Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints.

  • Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling.

  • Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners.

  • Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements.

  • Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network.

Who You Are

  • A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time.

  • A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems.

  • Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly.

  • Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods.

  • An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress.

Why Join Orakl

  • Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions.

  • Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together.

  • Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data.

  • Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions.

  • Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme.

  • Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support.

  • Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

  2. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity.

  3. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue.

  4. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership.

  5. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions.

description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

 L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

 

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche  articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur. 

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de neutralité carbone de la France.

Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600).

 

Ce recrutement est au cœur de la stratégie d’innovation de Mines Saint-Etienne pour permettre à un brevet IMT de se concrétiser en une technologie permettant de capter le CO2 des fumées industrielles, et de contribuer ainsi à l’atteinte de l’objectif Français de Neutralité carbone

·           Vous assurez le développement d’un pilote de captage du CO2,

·           Vous participez au transfert de technologie entre une méthodologie brevetée et la spin-off Carbon Cage,

·           Vous contribuez à un enjeu majeur de notre société,

·           Vous rendez compte l’équipe GasHyDyn qui soutient les développements méthodologiques, et vous interagissez au quotidien avec sa spin-off Carbon Cage.

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

·         Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent,

Et idéalement :

·         Titulaire d’une thèse

·         Junior accepté : [oui]

•      Une expérience significative sur le domaine des clathrates hydrates

•      Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1)

Vos atouts supplémentaires :

•           Capacité à travailler dans un contexte international et multiculturel

•           Capacité à travailler avec une startup

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver :

· Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain

· Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

· Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail.

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens.

title: Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer
Product Manager (English/French)
Embedded System Lead Engineer
description:
Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR

Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.


The role

As Embedded System Lead Engineer, you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it.

What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget.

You will lead their technical development, from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come.

These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge, on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role.

The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it.

What you'll own

  • Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications.

  • The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt.

  • Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS).

  • The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment.

  • Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore.

  • Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench.

  • Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units.

The hard problems you'll be solving

These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point:

  • Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling.

  • Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell.

  • Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible.

  • Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it.

  • Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean.

Who we're looking for

You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically:

  • 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world.

  • Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems. This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space.

  • Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack: electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal.

  • Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control.

  • Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do.

  • A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters.

  • Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it.

Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale.

Why join now

  • Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

  • A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

  • Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

  • AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

  • A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

title: Product Marketing Manager in Legal Tech (Zurich)
description:
Description

Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes.

You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind.


Your mission

1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence 

  • Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution.

  • Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy.

  • Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters.

  • Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo.

2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership 

  • Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer.

  • Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders).

  • Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice.

  • Own our thought leadership channels, including video, and decide what gets said. Write what can’t be delegated: founder posts, executive bylines, keynote scripts, board-level memos.

3. Sales & Customer-Facing Enablement 

  • Build the sales slides, briefings, one-pagers and competitive battlecards that make Sales and Customer Success more effective in every conversation.

  • Translate positioning and research into materials for specific deals, verticals and executive-level conversations.

  • Work directly with Sales and CS to find out what’s missing in the field. Build case studies and customer proof points that Sales actually uses, not ones that sit in a folder.

What We Want to Achieve Together

In 6 months: a flagship study that gets cited by competitors and customers. Sales armed with materials that actually get used in deals. A clear Legartis position that everyone in the company can repeat in 30 seconds.

In 12 months: Legartis recognized as one of the leading European voices on Legal AI, with a content and enablement engine, you plus the AI tools you direct, that outproduces companies with five times the headcount.


Your profile

  • Proven strategist: demonstrated success creating and executing marketing strategies.

  • Storyteller: you craft compelling materials about complex AI products for non-technical audiences.

  • Clear communicator: exceptional written and verbal communication with a strong visual sensibility.

  • Impact-driven: comfortable with experimentation and interpreting both quantitative and qualitative data.

  • AI-savvy: crafty with AI tools and automations — you use them daily and keep exploring what's new.

  • A track record where writing and thinking were central: journalism, industry or analyst research, strategy consulting, or senior product marketing with real strategic ownership. 4+ years in marketing, product marketing or a comparable strategic role at a SaaS company. Classic PMM experience (positioning, GTM, enablement) is a strong plus, not a hard requirement, if your thinking and writing are strong enough.

  • Fluent German and English, executive-level writing in both.


Why us?

  • Real editorial ownership over our voice and our position, not a content calendar handed down from someone else.

  • A platform to build your own visible profile as a voice in Legal AI.

  • Modern office in Leipzig or Berlin, hybrid setup, with regular presence in Zürich and team events such as hiking, dinners and offsites.

  • Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) participation.

  • Competitive salary, based on experience and seniority.


Process

  1. 30 min with our People & Operations Manager: cultural fit, understanding the role and your expectations.

  2. Positioning conversation with our Head of Product: bring a point of view on Legal AI and be ready to defend it live.

  3. Case study: show us something you’ve written or built, and how you’d turn it into a sales-ready asset.

  4. Meet the team in the office.

  5. Decision: if it’s mutual, we welcome you to the team!

How to Apply

Send us your CV, two or three writing or work samples you’re proud of, and a short note answering: what’s your sharpest point of view on where Legal AI is heading, and what’s the evidence?

title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description:
Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.

description:
Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract review. Today we build a holistic platform that changes how legal teams operate from review to negotiation, powered by our Legal Agent. When you join Legartis, you don't just take a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and legal experts. We don't chase hype; we build substance.


Your mission

This is not a classic legal role, and not a classic sales or product role. You operate at the intersection of Law, Revenue, and AI, where you are a lever, not a bottleneck: your job is to build the demos, playbooks, and standards that let the whole company scale, and to step into the calls where your expertise closes the gap.

1. Commercial impact. You help win and grow customers. You build and run demos that create a "wow" moment, join high-stakes prospect calls as the legal expert who speaks at eye level with GCs, and run our trials and workshops: onboarding sessions where customers solve their own use cases live, with you coaching. You turn objections into use cases and interest into next steps, and you enable our Sales team to tell the legal story without you in the room. You think of outcomes in terms of trial-to-signature conversion, adoption, expansion.

2. Customer transformation. Once a deal is signed, you make the value real by acting as a strategic sparring partner in onboarding: defining review requirements, tuning playbooks and prompts, and showing legal teams where Legartis delivers the highest ROI. You turn individual learnings into scalable standards and documentation.

3. Making the AI better. You work hands-on with the Legal Agent: prompting, testing, diagnosing where it breaks and why. You feed what you learn from customers back into Product and Engineering (playbook quality, test sets, edge cases) so the product improves with every customer.

4. Internal legal support. You don't just sell the tool; you use it. When necessary, you support Legartis as in-house counsel on contract reviews and specific legal questions.


Your profile

We are honest: people who combine all of this are rare. We hire for aptitude and attitude, assess hands-on in a case study, and train the rest side by side, in real customer work.

1. You can sell the product (key). Not in the cold-calling sense, but in the way a great expert sells: by making the customer succeed in front of their own team. Concretely, this means you can (or want to learn to):

  • Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result.
  • Coach the customer hands-on. In trials and hackathons, the customer drives and you navigate: you get them to enter their own real legal questions, create the first "wow" moment themselves, and build the habits (saved prompts, reusable workflows) that make them stay.
  • Turn objections into use cases. When a customer says "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves," you respond with a concrete path: a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative. You're straight about limits, because credibility is what closes.
  • Speak at eye level with GCs and legal teams asking sharp discovery questions, translating their friction points into what the product can do, and framing value in their language (ROI, risk, time saved).
  • Always leave with a next step. Trial licenses, a hackathon, a follow-up workshop, a scoped rollout conversation. You instinctively convert interest into momentum, and you remove friction ("we can make that happen") rather than adding process. Ideally you can point to moments where you influenced a deal, a renewal, or an expansion in any prior role.

2. Legal foundation. Solid legal training and hands-on experience with commercial contracts from in-house, law firm, or legal tech. You understand the "why" behind a clause and can teach that logic to an AI and to a customer. A German 2. Staatsexamen is welcome but not required: we explicitly encourage candidates with qualifications from other jurisdictions or non-traditional paths (e.g. law + IT).

3. Hands-on AI builder. You have spent serious time with LLMs, not as a spectator, but pushing them to their limits. You see prompting and evaluation as a craft and enjoy figuring out where AI systems break and how to fix them.

4. Ownership & communication. You can point to things you built, launched, or drove. You are structured enough to run projects with multiple stakeholders, and precise enough to know that a sharp prompt beats a thousand vague instructions. Excellent German and English; other languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, revenue, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.

title: Value Strategist
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

This is a senior individual contributor role within our global Revenue organization, spanning the full customer lifecycle from early sales conversations through proof of concept, deployment, renewal, and expansion. You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

In this role you will

  • Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

  • Build our global value strategy. Develop the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, discovery approaches, and playbooks that define how ElevenLabs approaches value across industries and use cases.

  • Scale what works. Turn bespoke work with our largest customers into repeatable approaches that enable our Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial teams to articulate and measure value without requiring bespoke support for every customer.

  • Identify where ElevenLabs can have the greatest impact. Develop a deep understanding of a customer's business, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities to determine which use cases have the greatest potential and why.

  • Quantify the opportunity. Build rigorous financial and operational models that translate ElevenLabs use cases into measurable outcomes across revenue, cost, productivity, customer experience, and other relevant dimensions.

  • Define how value will be proven. Establish success metrics and measurement approaches for proofs of concept and deployments so that customers and ElevenLabs have a shared understanding of what success looks like from the outset.

  • Measure value realization. Partner with customers and internal teams after deployment to understand the impact ElevenLabs is delivering, identify gaps between expected and realized value, and determine where additional opportunities exist.

  • Support expansion and long-term customer value. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.

  • Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.

  • Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.

  • Influence senior stakeholders. Communicate complex analysis simply and credibly, and engage with senior leaders internally and externally when the opportunity requires it.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of relevant experience across operating roles, strategy, management consulting, analytics, finance, customer strategy, or other roles requiring rigorous business problem solving.

  • Strong operating judgment. You understand how businesses work and can quickly get underneath a customer's operating model, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities.

  • Exceptional analytical ability. You can personally build sophisticated financial and operational models, work with incomplete or imperfect information, make assumptions explicit, and turn analysis into decisions.

  • Structured problem solving. You are comfortable starting with an ambiguous question such as "Where could AI create the most value in this business?" and developing a rigorous approach to answering it.

  • Customer credibility. You can work directly with customers across functions and levels, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and establish trust quickly.

  • Commercial judgment. You understand how business value connects to technology investment decisions and can partner closely with Revenue teams while maintaining an objective, customer-first perspective.

  • Excellent communication. You can distill complex analysis into a clear point of view and communicate it effectively in writing and verbally, from working teams through senior executives.

  • A builder mentality. You are excited to start by doing the work yourself, learn from customers, and turn what works into scalable methodologies and tools.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You can move quickly across industries, customer types, and use cases while maintaining a high bar for analytical rigor.

  • Ability to operate globally. You are comfortable partnering with teams and customers across regions and traveling when valuable for customer work.

  • Willingness to travel. Must be willing and able to travel up to 10% of the time.

Bonus points

  • Experience in strategy or management consulting, particularly in operational transformation, technology, customer experience, or growth.

  • Experience as an operator within a technology company or other fast-moving business.

  • Experience working on AI, automation, customer experience, or technology-enabled business transformation.

  • Experience developing business cases, value frameworks, or analytical methodologies that were ultimately scaled beyond an individual project or customer.

  • Experience working with enterprise customers on complex, cross-functional initiatives.

Location

This is a global role within the Revenue organization. The role can be based in San Francisco or remotely, with the option to work from our San Francisco office.

You will work with customers and ElevenLabs teams across regions and should expect travel for customer meetings and onsite work when it meaningfully advances the work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

The Role

As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware.

The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one.

This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes.

What You'll Work On

  • Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities.

  • Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather.

  • Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer.

  • Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts.

  • Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions.

  • Apply solid engineering practices: code review, version control, reproducible experiments and clear documentation.

Who We're Looking For

You don't need every item below, but you should meet the core requirements and bring depth in at least one area of the autonomy stack. You'll join a small team that moves fast, expects ownership, and holds work to the standard of running on live customer sites.

Your Background

  • Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD, or completed a Master's degree within the last year, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.

  • Strong coding skills in Python.

  • Hands-on experience with ROS 2.

  • Comfortable using Linux, Docker and Git in your workflows.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with physical robots, ideally mobile or legged.

  • Experience with lidar or camera processing, SLAM, or sensor fusion.

  • Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo or MuJoCo.

  • Publications or competition results in robotics (ICRA, IROS, RSS, CoRL).

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

 

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

 

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

 

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

 

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

 

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

 

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

title: Sr. Delivery Solutions Architect
Delivery Solutions Architect
Senior Consultant, Data & AI
Enterprise Sales Lead - Healthcare
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
In healthcare, the phone is still the front door, and call volume keeps rising while the people answering it are harder to hire and keep. You'll own our North America enterprise motion across providers, payers, and life sciences, helping health organizations put agents in front of patients, members, and clinicians that are safe, fast, and fit the systems they already run. You'll have the mandate to build the playbook and the team.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the enterprise healthcare function across health systems, payers, and pharma/medtech: strategy, pipeline, forecast, process, execution

  • Define the enterprise ICP, sales methodology, and a repeatable motion for each segment

  • Build and lead a high-performing enterprise sales team

  • Land and expand with large health systems, health plans, and life sciences companies

  • Work through BAAs, security review, and AI governance boards (and MLR review for pharma), starting compliance conversations in week one

  • Partner with our Forward Deployed Engineers to scope integrations with the EHR, claims, and telephony systems customers already run

  • Help customers pick one high-volume starting point (scheduling, reminders, after-hours coverage, benefits and claims status, HCP support) and prove it before scaling

  • Build a reference network of healthcare peers that buyers can call

  • Lead executive briefings, events, and high-stakes negotiations

  • Bring a sharp view of the competitive landscape, including build-vs-buy, platform bundlers, and vertical point solutions, to positioning and strategy

  • Set the bar for sales culture, integrity, and customer-first execution

Requirements:

  • Proven enterprise sales leadership in a high-growth, product-led tech company (AI/ML strongly preferred)

  • Track record selling to health systems, payers, or life sciences, with fluency in HIPAA, BAAs, and long, multi-stakeholder cycles

  • Experience building and scaling sales teams from the ground up

  • Seven-figure enterprise deals and complex sales cycles

  • Ability to be strategic and hands-on at once

  • Executive presence at C-suite and board levels

  • Collaborative, humble, and driven

  • Passion for the transformative potential of conversational AI

Remote-first in the United States, with a strong preference for New York or San Francisco, where we have office spaces.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: PCB/RF Design Engineer
description:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

Join us as a RF/PCB Design Engineer to drive the physical realization of our next-generation 3D quantum hardware architecture - hardware that operates from room temperature down to millikelvin conditions inside a dilution refrigerator. You will own the design of critical microwave components, create high-density cryo-compatible PCB layouts, and build novel packaging solutions for large-scale QPUs. Working at the intersection of hardware and software, you'll also help streamline our development by embedding design processes into automated workflows.

What you'll be doing

  • Component & Mechanical Design: Design critical electromechanical components that form the chief interface of our QPUs and TWPAs. You will work as part of the packaging team and interface closely with the Product design team.

  • Precision Engineering: Utilise CAD to design PCBs, silicon chip layout and PCB-to-chip interconnect within the vertical VIO architecture.

  • RF/Microwave Design: Solve complex challenges related to insertion loss, impedance matching, and cross-talk at the PCB and package levels.

  • Cryogenic Integration & Testing: Design for and validate performance across the full temperature range from room temperature to millikelvin — accounting for thermal cycling, differential contraction, and material behavior at cryogenic temperatures, and running cooldown/characterization tests in dilution refrigerators.

Your Profile

  • Education: BSc or MSc in Electrical Engineering with a focus on PCB design, layout, and RF/Microwave Engineering.

  • Experience: 4+ years of hands-on PCB design experience utilizing tools such as KiCAD, Altium Designer, and Cadence to deliver high-quality board designs. Experience with diverse materials such as cofired ceramic boards (LTCC, HTCC) is a plus.

  • Cryogenic Applications: Hands-on experience designing or testing hardware for cryogenic environments - e.g., dilution refrigerators, cryostats, or low-temperature RF/microwave systems.

  • Core EE Fundamentals: Solid understanding of developing schematics, electro-mechanical interfaces, RF layout trades, temperature dependent behavior, shielding, signal integrity, and impedance analysis.

Nice to Have:

  • Packaging & Interconnects: Background in high-density interconnects, high frequency flex interconnects, 3D packaging, or advanced integration.

  • Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with superconducting technologies is a strong plus.

  • RF Characterization: Practical experience with RF testing and measurements using VNA and related laboratory equipment.

title: Quantum Design Engineer
description:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

As a Quantum Design Engineer in our R&D team, you’ll be at the heart of advancing the performance and scalability of superconducting quantum processors. You’ll lead the design of next-generation qubit chips and modular, scalable QPU architecture, working from on-chip subsystem architecture to EM simulations, frequency allocation, crosstalk management, packaging, and interconnect strategies.

You’ll also design and optimise nonreciprocal superconducting circuits, such as isolators and parametric amplifiers that will drive robust, high-fidelity readout chains. These designs will enhance readout signal-to-noise ratio and stability, feeding into our next-gen readout modules and ensuring seamless coupling with the qubit layer.

This role is highly collaborative: you’ll work in a tight feedback loop with experimentalists and device engineers to transform measurement insights into rapid design iterations, pushing performance, coherence, yield, and manufacturability across the full qubit stack.

What you’ll be doing

  • Design and simulate cutting-edge quantum hardware to improve performance, coherence, and scalability.

  • Develop high-performance, manufacturable device architectures that accelerate R&D cycles and increase qubit fidelity and yield.

  • Architect and optimize the layout of nonreciprocal superconducting circuits such as parametric amplifiers, targeting robust performance under cryogenic conditions.

  • Interpret simulation results and correlate with experimental data to guide iterative design improvements.

  • Collaborate across teams to ensure rapid design-to-test cycles, connecting theory with experiment.

  • Automate the design pipeline using Python, enabling parametric device generation, simulation sweeps, and data post-processing.

Your profile

  • MSc in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or related field, with 2+ years of industry experience or a PhD with relevant hands-on work

  • Strong Python skills for automating designs, controlling simulations, and analyzing data

  • Experience with EM simulation and chip design tools (e.g. Ansys HFSS-Q3D, KLayout); Git and Qiskit-Metal familiarity is a plus

  • Knowledge of cQED devices and superconducting circuit design is a strong advantage

  • Experience designing nonreciprocal superconducting circuits (e.g. parametric amplifiers) or advanced readout techniques is highly valued

  • Solid grasp of microwave engineering, quantum noise sources, and fabrication methods
