title: Business Development Representative
description:
About Evervault Evervault provides online card payment infrastructure primarily to companies building card payments into their products, as well as to sophisticated merchants who manage payment routing in-house. Best-in-class companies like Ramp, Overwolf, and Modern Treasury build their products on top of Evervault.

Beyond that, we are extending our core encryption technology to secure sensitive data for use cases outside of card payments, including banking, healthcare, identity, crypto, and more. Our mission is to become the clearinghouse for sensitive data, so companies can move data freely between systems without the compliance and security overhead.

The Role Traditional BDR tactics are broken. We need someone who can identify and engage CTOs, CPOs, VPs of ProdEng and founders at 100-5,000 person companies during their moments of genuine need - not with generic cold emails, but through strategic timing and thoughtful outreach.

What Success Looks Like

  • 16 Qualified Opportunities generated per quarter

  • Making inroads into target accounts via strategic stakeholder mapping, cold calling, in person events, and email/socials to our target personas

  • Becoming an SME in the card payments domain

What You'll Do

  • Signal-Based Prospecting: Track the moments that create a need for card infrastructure, such as a company adding a second PSP, expanding into new geographies, launching card issuing or embedded payments, hiring its first payments engineer or compliance lead, or facing a PCI DSS audit or renewal.

  • Payments-Led Research: Map a target account's current payment stack (processors, vault, checkout, 3DS provider) and pinpoint where they're likely feeling pain, whether that's PCI scope weighing on engineering, vendor lock-in with a single processor, declining authorization rates, or rising fraud and chargeback exposure.

  • Relevant Outreach: Engage CTOs, CPOs, VPs of Product and Engineering, and founders through calls, email, LinkedIn, and warm intros, with messaging tied to outcomes they care about: reducing PCI compliance burden, owning card data to route freely across processors, lifting auth rates with network tokens and card account updater, and bringing down fraud and chargebacks with 3DS.

  • Cold Calling: Run consistent call blocks into target accounts to start conversations with technical buyers and learn how they handle card data today.

  • Domain Expertise: Build a working knowledge of card payments, including tokenization, payment orchestration, network tokens, 3DS, PCI DSS v4.0, and the card network rules on disputes, so you can hold credible first conversations with technical executives.

  • Community and Events: Build relationships in fintech, payments, and founder/CTO communities, and help turn in-person events and meetups into pipeline in target markets.

  • Partner-Sourced Pipeline: Work with VCs, PSPs, consultants, and complementary vendors to source warm introductions into accounts where Evervault fits.

  • Pipeline Handoff: Qualify opportunities against our criteria and hand them to AEs with clear context on the prospect's stack, pain points, and why now.

You're Perfect If You Have

  • 1-2 years of BDR experience, preferably selling an API-based solution to technical personas

  • Track record of research-heavy, personalized outreach over high-volume activities

  • Understanding of the pain points of companies processing a high volume of card transactions

  • Genuine curiosity about connecting business’ payments problems to technical solutions

About this role

Turns product and customer insight into shipped things like customer stories, tools, reports, courses, and community. You’ll tell our audience how customers use and get the best out of Evervault.

In March 2026, we raised $25m in our Series B led by Ribbit Capital. We’ve got a truly incredible and differentiated product that customers love. Your role is to help us tell that story.

You will join our “fuel room,” working closely with product marketing, content, and design. Our CEO, Shane, is heavily involved, whether it’s brainstorming ideas, sharing his wisdom, or being the face/voice for the content we produce; it’s a unique opportunity to get this much access.

The ultimate goal of this role is to own the understanding and communication of how our customers actually use us and how they can get the most from Evervault.

This means becoming the expert on the different business models and customer types we serve; how they operate, how they use Evervault today, and how they could get more out of us.

What you’ll do

You’ll be regularly talking to customers, hunting for interesting stories to tell, and creative ways to tell them.

By spending time with customer success and solutions engineering, you’ll add color to our target segments, gaining an intimate understanding of the characteristics that shape what they need from Evervault and how they use us.

You'll get into the weeds of our solutions with product and engineering, connecting what you know about customers to what's technically possible, so you can show new and existing customers the best way to get value from Evervault.

Armed with all that research, you'll be creative in how you communicate. Great writing will be a staple, and there will be blogs, social posts, etc. But we want someone who can explore new formats and ways to achieve your goal. Maybe it's hosting customer workshops to share best practices around a common pain point, creating YouTube videos as part of a learning module, or building a benchmark tool using the swathes of payment data we collect.

What you are

  • 3+ years of work experience. Backgrounds we like include product, product marketing, developer, technical writing, and solutions engineering.

  • Technically competent. Ideally, you’ve got a computer science or mechanical engineering-type background, or hobby developer experience.

  • Exceptional English writing and speaking skills.

  • Thinks like a journalist. You instinctively ask naive questions without embarrassment until you get an answer that is actually interesting.

  • Highly creative. Knowing what to say is part of the battle. Figuring out how to say it in a way that’s cool and interesting is something we’re really in the market for. Think Posthog Lite.

  1. Competitive base

  2. Stock options with extendable exercise window

  3. Work from our office in London

  4. Flexible working hours

  5. Generous vacation days

  6. Private health insurance

  7. Catered lunch

Logistics

  1. Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in our office 3 days a week, Tuesday-Thursday.

title: Product Designer
description:
We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible 💙

The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.

We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.

We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀

⛩️ Our Principles

Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1:

  1. 💙 Care deeply

  2. 🏋️‍♀️ Work hard

  3. 🤝 Be your word

  4. 💬 Trust in radical truth and transparency

  5.  🚀 Do your life's best work

  6. 🥳 Find the fun

Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook.

The role

We're hiring a mid-level Product Designer to work directly with our CEO to own the design of the Bookable Navigator Inbox: this is the place where GP practice teams receive, triage and act on every patient request. It's used all day by receptionists, care navigators and clinicians, and every rough edge costs them precious time with patients.

To be clear: this isn't a senior or leadership role. It's for a designer who has spend 3-5 years shipping within fast-paced product teams and wants to accelerate their career. You'll have a lot of ownership, be expected to stay close to users, and work closely with engineering. If you are hungry, want to work hard, and want a role of a lifetime, we'd love to hear from you.

What you'll do

Get close to users

  • Talk to practice staff regularly: run interviews, sit in on real shifts, and watch how the Inbox gets used

  • Research and scope product tickets before they reach engineering, so we build the right thing

  • Become the user: dogfood the product until you know its friction better than anyone

Use data

  • Dig into product metrics to find where people get stuck, then turn that into design work

  • Measure whether what you shipped actually made things better

Design and ship

  • Take ideas from scrappy MVP through to polished, high-fidelity design

  • Make things simple, beautiful and usable, for people working under real time pressure

  • Work side by side with engineers, from first sketch to what goes live

  • Use AI tools like Claude every day to research, prototype and move faster

About you

  • You've cut your teeth on at least two great products, shipped and used by real people

  • You've worked in a product team, and you've worked at a startup

  • You're obsessed with UI and think about design constantly, down to the spacing on a button

  • You're excited about talking to users and getting close to the problem

  • You have the fire to improve: you seek out feedback and want to get much better quickly

  • You're comfortable with numbers and can make a case from data

  • You already use AI tools in your workflow

Bonus: the best candidates will think like a product manager. You ask why before how, can scope a problem down to what matters, and have opinions about what to build next. We'll explore this in the interview process.

Progression

As AI changes how software gets built, the line between design and product is blurring, and this role sits right on the edges. You'll start owning the Inbox experience, and grow towards owning product decisions end to end.

We want people who could one day found their own company. Here you'll get the reps to do it: real users, real problems in the NHS, and the freedom to work directly with our CEO to shape what we build.

The details

  • Salary: competitive, plus equity

  • Location: London (Stratford), in the office 4 days a week with 1 day (Wed) working from home

💙 A bit about us

💙 We’re all NHS staff. We’re inside-outsiders. Trusted with one of the biggest datasets in the world.

🏥 Our office is within a GP practice. This is our unfair advantage. Got a question? Pop down the corridor. Want to learn how your work affects real patients? Pop downstairs to reception.

💪🏼 4 days in the office and 1 day WFH (for most roles). We highly prioritise in-person communication and prefer candidates who want to work 4+ days a week in the office. Our anchor days are Mon, Tues, Thurs and Fri. Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house every day when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🌀 We work in growth cycles. Every 8 weeks we do the same set of activities. 1 week outside of Business-as-Usual to research, strategise, plan our work. 7 weeks to knuckle down and deliver it.

🤝 We’re highly collaborative. One of the benefits of a high trust team is we often work autonomously, but as a team we’re very collaborative by nature. Two heads are often better than one, and we frequently lean on each other to solve problems together.

🤜🏽 We’re backed by industry leaders. We’re on the DigitalHealth.London Accelerator, backed by the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Program, winners of the London Business School Healthtech Challenge, Innovate UK, and Y Combinator (S23).

🚀 An opportunity for real upside

💉 Paid volunteer days. We offer an additional 2 paid days off per year where you can give back to your mission of choice.

🎢 Every 8 weeks we take a day off to socialise as a team. In the past we’ve hiked box hill, raved at All Points East and spent one rainy day at Thorpe park. This works out as 6 working days a year.

📚 Learning budget of £250 annually and time off to spend it - we care about this; this is flexible and based on need but everyone will receive a yearly allocation towards their continual growth.

🍽️ Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🥡 Team takeaways every Monday night

🥗 Health and fitness budget of £60 per month - see more here

🧘‍♂️ An additional 7 days of paid leave is available if you want to take time to learn how to meditate.

💫 Tooling; You’ll have your choice of operating systems and any additional tools you need to do your best work (e.g. keyboard, additional monitors, mouse etc). If you’re on our Engineering teams you’ll receive the latest MacBook Pro and our Growth & Ops teams receives a MacBook Air.

🩺 We know health and family come first which is why we have a generous sick leave policy with additional days that can be taken for mental health leave.

✈️ We prioritise time outside of work to bond, once a year we’ll holiday together! Destination chosen by popular vote. In 2025, we spent 8 days in a surf camp in France!

👎 No private medical insurance, because we believe in the NHS and we are here to improve it!

🐥 Parental leave: Post passing probation it is: statutory - 6 weeks 90% pay then, SMP for 33 weeks; if you've been an employee for a year: 12 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 27 weeks; and if you have been here for 2 years: 18 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 21 weeks. This will improve over time. We also include up to £9,000 of childcare contribution for primary caregivers to support a five-day return where possible.

👪 Fertility leave. We understand how difficult a fertility journey can be. This is why we give an extra 5 days off per year if you or your partner are going through fertility treatment.

🐖 Pension - We operate a standard 3% employer contribution and employees auto-contribute 5% of their salary. We use Nest as our provider.

🏡 Local living benefit - A one-off benefit to support living closer to the office: £5,000 if you live within a 30-minute walk, or £2,500 within a 30-minute bike. It is optional, available immediately on signing, and not linked to performance or progression.

🚕 If you choose to work late in the office, you can expense dinner after 7pm and an Uber home after 9pm, or earlier if you feel unsafe travelling in the dark. This is optional and about wellbeing, not performance or expectations.

⛵️And of course, an adventure of a lifetime!

🌈 Inclusive & Diverse by Design

We care about building a product that is loved and a culture that is rich in perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds.

Our team represents more than ten different cultures. We come together every lunch time for a home cooked meal, rotated among team members!

We want everyone in our team to know that they belong. We are purposeful about this and are proactively building a company that is inclusive of all people; from race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodiversity, disability, colour, and national origin - essentially every type of diversity. We don’t just want people who fit in, we want them to fit together. We're active in continually improving the way we make this happen.

description:
Unleash AI Innovators, Securely

Software is being rewritten in real time. AI agents are starting to write more code than humans do, at a speed no security team has ever had to match, and that single shift is opening up the biggest opportunity our industry has seen in a decade. We're not bracing for it, we're building the company that owns it.

Snyk is building the next generation security platform where security isn't a set of tools people operate. It's a team of security agents working alongside your engineers, finding, fixing, and governing risk at the speed software is now built. These agents work alongside both the company build and the agents they adopt. Security stops being a queue of work waiting for people, and becomes a coordinated workforce companies direct and trust.

Job Summary

As Regional Partner Manager for the UK/I territory, you own the strategy, enablement, and performance of Snyk's strategic channel partners, and you recruit new regional security partners to grow our reach. You will align partners to Snyk's sales segmentation and work alongside our sales teams to build pipeline across the region. This role matters because AI is changing how software gets built, and our partners are how many customers will adopt secure AI development at scale.

About the Team

You will join Snyk's Partner organization, which builds and grows the channel and alliance relationships that extend Snyk's go-to-market. The team works closely with regional sales leadership to turn partner relationships into pipeline and revenue.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the partner strategy and business plan for the UK/I territory, including performance, pipeline, and revenue goals.

  • Partner with Snyk sales leadership and the broader team to build a joint plan and pipeline across the region.

  • Develop and embed Snyk into your partners' DevSecOps strategy and business plans, covering every aspect of the relationship.

  • Recruit and onboard regional, security-focused partners across key markets in the UK and Ireland.

  • Build and maintain an alliance partner plan, along with activity and performance reports.

  • Lead regular business performance and relationship reviews with partner and internal stakeholders.

  • Align partners to Snyk's sales segmentation and to the right Snyk sales teams.

  • Communicate clearly and consistently with partners and peers to build strong, lasting partnerships.

  • Represent Snyk at partner activities and events across the territory.

What you’ll bring

  • 5 or more years of channel sales experience, with a proven track record of selling with or through the security channel partner ecosystem in the US West region.

  • Experience working with regional channel partners such as Softcat and Computacenter is preferred.

  • A demonstrated record of solution selling and value-based selling.

  • A solid understanding of Snyk's solutions and the business value they deliver to both partners and customers.

  • Excellent presentation, written, and communication skills, with the ability to work across all levels of a partner organization.

  • High energy and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to travel up to 50% of the time for partner activities and events.

  • If this role excites you but you do not meet every requirement, please apply anyway. You might be the person we are looking for.

description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to shape some of the most important experiences in our marketplace. You'll own complex, high-impact problem spaces end to end, from ambiguous discovery through to shipped, measured outcomes and raise the bar for design craft and pace across the whole team.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with real influence. You'll partner directly with product and engineering leadership, mentor other designers, and set the standard for how design work gets done at Carwow.

A note on how we work: AI fluency is integral to the role. Our design team works AI-natively. We use Claude Design (and similar tools) to move from idea to high-quality prototype in hours, not weeks, and we expect designers at this level to be genuinely fluent in this way of working, not just curious about it. If you're still designing the way teams did in 2023, this probably isn't the right role. If you've rebuilt your workflow around AI and it's made you dramatically faster and more ambitious, we'd love to talk.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Own end-to-end design for a major problem space in our marketplace. Buying, selling, or dealer-facing products. from discovery and framing through to launch and iteration

  • Prototype at pace using AI design tools (Claude Design or equivalent), getting real, testable experiences in front of users and stakeholders early and often

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers, using AI-assisted workflows to close the gap between design intent and shipped product, ideally getting hands-on in code where it speeds things up

  • Set direction, not just execute: identify opportunities, make the case with evidence, and bring product and engineering partners with you

  • Raise the craft bar across the team through critique, mentorship, and by making your own work an example worth following

  • Champion AI-native ways of working. Sharing techniques, building reusable prompts and workflows, and helping the wider team level up

  • Ground decisions in evidence, combining user research, data, and rapid experimentation

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • A high degree of AI fluency. Hands-on, demonstrable experience using Claude Design (or an equivalent AI design/prototyping tool) as a core part of your workflow. This is critical to the role, and we'll want to see it in your portfolio and hear about it in interviews

  • Strong end-to-end craft: you can go from a fuzzy problem statement to polished, production-ready design, and everything you ship is considered

  • Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You make good decisions with incomplete information and iterate quickly

  • Excellent communication and influence: you can align senior stakeholders, tell a compelling story with your work, and hold your ground constructively

  • Experience mentoring designers and lifting the standard of a team|

STRONGLY PREFERRED SKILLS

In your first six months you'll have taken ownership of a significant problem space, shipped work that measurably moves a core metric, and become someone other designers seek out — both for the quality of your craft and for how you use AI tools to work at a pace and ambition level others want to copy.


WHY CARWOW?

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our award-winning Data Science team at a pivotal moment. Carwow operates a two-sided marketplace — connecting car buyers and sellers at scale — and data science sits at the heart of how we make that marketplace smarter, faster, and more valuable for everyone in it. In fact, we recently won GenAI initiative of the Year at the British Data Awards.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role working centrally across the business. You'll partner with teams spanning Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations — developing and deploying ML and AI solutions that drive outcomes across both sides of our marketplace. The problems you'll work on are genuinely varied: pricing models, propensity and demand signals that sharpen marketing spend, personalised recommendations for our web product and CRM, and LLM-powered solutions for operational challenges like document verification.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

title: Design Engineer
description:
About Aibidia

Aibidia is a fast-growing SaaS company transforming how multinational businesses manage transfer pricing. We're building intelligent, scalable software that simplifies complex tax and compliance processes, helping some of the world's largest organisations work more efficiently and confidently.

We're a team that values curiosity, ownership and pragmatic problem-solving. As we continue to evolve our products and embrace AI-native ways of working, we're looking for a Design Engineer to help shape the next generation of our platform.

The Role

We're looking for an AI-first Design Engineer who combines strong technical capabilities with a solid understanding of product design, UX and usability.

This is a hybrid role at the intersection of design and engineering. You'll work on complex, data-rich enterprise software, using modern AI tools to rapidly prototype, iterate and deliver intuitive product experiences.

We're not looking for someone who simply creates beautiful interfaces or follows traditional, lengthy design processes. We want someone who thinks systematically, understands how software is built and knows how to leverage AI to turn complex requirements into functional, user-friendly solutions.

You'll join a team that has already established an AI-first design system and modern ways of working. Rather than reinventing what's already in place, you'll build on these foundations, contributing to an evolving design system while helping us move towards faster, more iterative product development.

What You'll Do

Design, prototype and ship

  • Translate complex business requirements and user needs into intuitive, functional product experiences.

  • Rapidly prototype and iterate on new features using AI-powered tools, getting working solutions in front of users early.

  • Work closely with Product Managers, Engineers and domain experts to take ideas from concept through to implementation.

  • Balance usability, technical feasibility and speed of delivery, knowing when to iterate and when a solution is good enough to ship.

  • Design for complex, data-heavy workflows where clarity, efficiency and accuracy matter more than visual embellishment.

Build with an AI-first mindset

  • Use AI tools such as Claude, Figma and MCP integrations as a core part of your design and development workflow.

  • Experiment with emerging AI technologies, agents and workflows to continuously improve how we build products.

  • Apply sound design and engineering judgement to AI-generated outputs, ensuring quality, usability and consistency.

Contribute to our design system

  • Build on and contribute to our existing AI-first design system, ensuring consistency and scalability across the product.

  • Understand and apply design system principles, including components, design tokens, spacing, layouts, accessibility and interaction patterns.

  • Identify opportunities to improve components, documentation and AI-assisted design workflows.

Collaborate and validate

  • Work directly with users and internal stakeholders to understand problems, validate ideas and gather feedback.

  • Take a lean, iterative approach to product development, prioritising early validation over lengthy discovery cycles.

  • Collaborate closely with Engineering to ensure designs are technically achievable and can be efficiently implemented.

  • Continuously refine solutions based on user feedback, technical constraints and evolving business needs.

What We're Looking For

  • A hybrid design and engineering background, with hands-on coding capabilities and a strong understanding of UX, UI and usability principles.

  • Experience using modern AI tools as an integral part of your workflow, with a genuine interest in AI-assisted design, prototyping and development.

  • Strong systems thinking, with an understanding of how scalable design systems, reusable components and technical frameworks work together.

  • Experience contributing to design systems, with knowledge of design tokens, component libraries, accessibility and established UI patterns.

  • Experience working directly with codebases, GitHub and modern frontend technologies, rather than operating solely within traditional design tools.

  • Experience designing or building complex, data-dense B2B SaaS, enterprise or workflow-driven products.

  • Experience working in a startup or scaleup environment, where priorities evolve, teams are lean and speed of execution matters.

  • Strong product judgement and the ability to balance user needs, business requirements and technical constraints.

  • A curious, adaptable mindset and enthusiasm for experimenting with emerging technologies and new ways of working.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, tax technology, compliance or other complex, regulated industries.

  • Exposure to both early-stage startups and larger, more established software organisations.


Why Join Aibidia?

  • Build the future of AI-first product development: Help shape how AI is embedded into the way we design, prototype and ship software.

  • Solve genuinely complex problems: Work on sophisticated enterprise software where thoughtful design and usability have a meaningful impact.

  • Make an impact: Join a lean, collaborative team where your ideas, technical judgement and contributions directly influence the product.

  • Work with modern tools: Experiment with emerging AI technologies and continuously improve how products are built.

  • Grow with us: Be part of a scaling international SaaS business that's challenging traditional approaches to tax technology.

Benefits & Perks:

  • 💰 Share in Aibidia’s success – Enjoy a competitive compensation and incentive package that rewards your contribution.

  • 🏡 Flexible, hybrid working – Flexible working hours and a hybrid policy designed to support how you work best.

  • 🩺 Comprehensive healthcare – A healthcare package to support you and your wellbeing.

  • 💚 Wellbeing that matters – A genuine focus on physical and mental wellbeing, supported by our internal Health & Wellbeing Committee.

  • 🎉 Time to celebrate together – Regular team socials, including our much-loved summer and winter parties.

  • 💻 The best tools for the job – Access to the latest technology to help you do your best work.

  • 🚀 Invest in your growth – Performance-based development is part of our culture, with a dedicated learning budget for every employee.

  • 🌍 Make an impact globally – Join a fast-growing global SaaS company using technology to transform a traditionally complex industry.

  • 🤝 Low hierarchy, high collaboration – Work in an open, collaborative environment where ideas are valued and everyone has the opportunity to make an impact.

 

We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity, we want you to bring you, no matter your background, gender, race or sexual orientation!

Please note, we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. To be considered, you’ll need to show proof of your eligibility to work in the country.

title: Platform Security Engineer
description:
At Scality, we build software that stores and protects the world’s most critical data — running on Linux, inside some of the largest infrastructures on the planet, at exabyte scale, for organizations that cannot afford to fail.

We are looking for a Platform Security Engineer to join our platform and delivery team in Paris. This is a new seat, and it exists because security work needs dedicated capacity. Absorbed as background tasks between feature tickets, it never gets the focus it deserves. You would be that dedicated capacity.

This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound.


About Scality

Scality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox.

Industry recognition:

  • Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception
  • #1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors
  • Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category
  • Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA

About the team

You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution).

The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers.


How We Build

We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day.

We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build.

If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it.

One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all.


How This Role Works

Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team.

  • Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one.
  • The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside.
  • You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists.
  • You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them.
  • You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft.

    • The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it.


Your First Missions

Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year.

1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked

Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending.

Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives.

  • A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration
  • Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives
  • Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs
  • Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks
  • A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy
  • Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable
  • A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira
  • AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships

    • Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks.

    2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS

    SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship:

    • A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution
    • Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry)
    • Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds
    • Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline
    • Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on
    • Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets

      • You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes.


What We Are Looking For

This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat.

Required

  • Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI
  • Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below
  • Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase
  • A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real
  • Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment
  • Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it
  • The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed
  • The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend
  • French — the team works in French day to day
  • Written communication skills in English

    • Nice to Have

    • CVE triage, CVSS scoring, or vulnerability management experience
    • Reading vendor advisories and understanding vendor triage — NVD, RHSA, Red Hat severity and will-not-fix calls
    • Supply-chain security tooling — SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX), scanners (Trivy, Grype, Syft), artifact signing
    • RPM packaging or Linux distribution internals
    • SELinux policy work
    • CI/CD systems, especially GitHub Actions
    • RHEL / Rocky Linux (versions 8 and 9)
    • Containers (Docker, containerd, systemd units)
    • Ansible or Salt
    • Awareness of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, or FIPS 140-3
    • Familiarity with S3 or object storage concepts
    • Serious use of AI coding tools in a real workflow — Claude Code or equivalent, beyond autocomplete

      • To Be Clear About Scope

      This is a software engineering role with a security mandate. It is not a SOC or incident-response analyst position, not a penetration-testing role, and not a GRC or compliance-documentation role. If what you want is to build the tooling and harden the system yourself, in code, you are in the right place.


What We Offer
  • Dedicated focus. Security is your job here, not the thing you get to after the sprint work is done
  • Clear direction, and a say in it. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering, and the team is accountable for delivering them. You would not be inventing the agenda on your own, you would help shape what goes on it, and you would be part of making it stick
  • A network of peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams, working the same problems on different perimeters
  • Work that compounds. Customer security questions are a permanent obligation, so every assessment you make reusable and every check you automate keeps paying back, release after release
  • Modern tooling, actually adopted. Claude Code in every engineer’s hands, and a real say in how AI reshapes our build and delivery chain
  • A rare combination: security work with the leverage of owning the whole stack, down to our own Linux distribution
  • Mentorship from senior engineers with deep expertise across Linux, storage, packaging, and distributed systems — you will not be the only person who understands your perimeter
  • A long-term growth path toward becoming your team’s security reference and a senior voice in the network
  • Work that ships to production and runs at exabyte scale, in banking, healthcare, and government
  • Standard French benefits: meal vouchers, Navigo subsidy, mutuelle

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Nous transformons la façon dont le monde mange et fait ses courses en rendant leur accès plus pratique et agréable. Nous connectons les consommateurs, les restaurants, les magasins et les cyclistes. Nous donnons à chaque personne la possibilité d'acheter ce qu'elles veulent, comme elles le veulent, quand elles le veulent et où elles le veulent.

Nous sommes une entreprise axée sur la technologie, à l'avant-garde d'un secteur qui connaît une des expansions les plus rapides au monde. Nous avançons rapidement, valorisons l'autonomie, et sommes toujours en recherche de nouvelles idées et de personnes talentueuses pour nous rejoindre!

Tes principales missions :  

  • Gérer un portefeuille de restaurants clés sur des zones matures, où l'expertise et l'attention au détail font toute la différence.
  • Développer des partenariats privilégiés et durables en devenant le point de contact expert de votre zone et en mettant à profit vos connaissances Food Tech.
  • Optimiser la performance de vos comptes grâce à un accompagnement personnalisé, construit sur le long terme et nourri par la data.
  • Analyser les résultats de vos restaurants, identifier les leviers d'amélioration et recommander des actions concrètes à votre manager tout en restant agile et ouvert à la nouveauté.
  • Proposer et mettre en place des campagnes marketing et promotionnelles ciblées pour booster l'attractivité de vos restaurants partenaires.

title: Scientist II Machine Learning Engineer (LLM & GenAI Specialist)
description:
About us

Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.
Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity.
K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners.

Position is based in our Paris offices or remotely in France, UK, or Germany.

Please submit your CV in English

About the role:

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Scientist II Machine Learning Engineer to design, develop, and deploy cutting-edge AI solutions. In this role, you will focus heavily on Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and Advanced Deep Learning architectures.

You will bridge the gap between experimental data science and production-ready ML systems. Working closely with our Data Science and Engineering teams, you will scale complex models, optimize training and inference pipelines, and leverage cloud ecosystems to deliver robust biomedical solutions. Experience handling health, clinical, or omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, etc.) is a major plus.

 

In particular, you will:

  • Develop scalable machine learning libraries, tooling, and research workflows in close partnership with research and data scientists.

  • Shape research infrastructure requirements and drive tool and software choices in collaboration with the platform team.

  • Champion software engineering best practices across the team, enabling researchers and scientists to write maintainable, testable, efficient, and scalable code.

  • Design and enhance systems for experiment tracking, reproducibility, and end-to-end model lifecycle management.

  • Contribute to and accelerate the rapid prototyping of novel models, helping bridge early research and robust implementation.

  • Other Ad-hoc responsibilities, tasks and projects assigned by the management.

  

About you

Required qualifications / experience:

  • Education: Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related quantitative field with a strong focus on ML/AI.

  • Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in software development with Python and a proven track record of deploying deep learning models into production.

  • ML/DL Frameworks & Ecosystems: Deep understanding of machine learning algorithms, statistical methods, and deep learning frameworks. Mastery of PyTorch or TensorFlow.

  • LLM Specialization: Deep understanding of Transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, and the latest breakthroughs in Generative AI. Extensive experience with Hugging Face, with knowledge in agentic workflows and RAG.

  • Cloud & MLOps: Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and SageMaker

  • Software Engineering Culture: Strong engineering practices including version control, comprehensive testing, CI/CD, and containerization (Docker).

  • Workflow Optimization: Experience with distributed computing, distributed training strategies for massive datasets, and optimization of ML workflows (e.g., vLLM).

Preferred qualifications/bonus:

  • Domain Expertise: Experience working with clinical or omics data (e.g., genomic sequencing, transcriptomics, electronic health records) and medical imaging processing and analysis.

  • Contributions to open-source ML projects or research publications.

Soft skills and culture add:

  • Collaborative Mindset: Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to analyze complex technical challenges.

  • Strong communication skills: The ability to explain technical concepts to various stakeholders.

  • Mentorship: Proactive approach to debugging complex distributed systems, mentoring team members in writing high-quality, maintainable software, and driving a strong technical culture.

  • Autonomy: primarily autonomous and capable of being given tasks without excessive detail, able to figure out what to do and execute.

#LI-HB1

 

What we offer

  • Flexible work organization

  • Friendly and informal working environment

  • Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds

Recruitment Process & Security

  • Please complete the form and submit your CV.

  • Owkin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status or on the basis of disability.

  • Owkin is a great place to work. As a coveted workplace we are, unfortunately, vulnerable to recruitment phishing scams. We urge all job seekers and candidates to be wary of potential scams. Most of these have individuals posing as representatives of prominent companies, including Owkin, with the aim of obtaining personal, sensitive, or financial information from applicants. These scams prey upon an individual’s desire to obtain a job and can sometimes “feel” like a genuine recruitment process. Some red flags are identified below. Should you encounter a recruitment process that claims to be for Owkin but is not consistent with the below, please do not provide any personal or financial information:

  • Legitimate Owkin recruitment processes include communication with candidates through recognized professional networks, such as LinkedIn.

  • Communication is always through an official Owkin email address (from the @owkin.com domain), over the phone or through our applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).

  • The Owkin talent team do use platforms such as LinkedIn and Job Teaser, however if you have any concern or doubt about this contact, please ask for them to send an email from @Owkin.com.

  • The Owkin talent team will not solicit personal data from candidates during the application phase including, but not limited to, date of birth, social security numbers, or bank account information;

  • Legitimate Owkin interviews may be conducted over the phone, in person, or via an approved enterprise videoconferencing service (Google Meets). They will not occur via Signal, Telegram or Messenger

  • Owkin offers of employment are based on merit and only extended once a candidate has interviewed with members of the talent and hiring team. Offers will be extended both verbally and in written format.

If you think that you have been a victim of fraud,

  • Check the identity of the talent team on LinkedIn

  • Check our senior team on our website https://owkin.com/team/

  • Check the existence of the position on our website: https://www.owkin.com/careers#current-opportunities

  • Notify Owkin's recruitment unit at this address contact the following authorities:

    • [FR] https://internet-signalement.gouv.fr/

    • [UK] https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/reporting-fraud-and-cyber-crime

    • [US] https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/

title: Senior Software Engineer — AI-Native Engineering (XTM Foundation)
description:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is genuinely, deeply convinced that AI is transforming the way software gets built, and who wants to make that transformation happen at Filigran.

We are looking for an engineer first. This isn't a "we bought Copilot, please roll it out" role, and it isn't only a tooling or development role either: part of the job is building, part of it is trying things on real work, measuring them and telling teams honestly what works and what doesn't. This is a practitioner role for someone who has already lived this shift, who experiments constantly, who knows what works and what doesn't, and who can bring 60 engineers along on that journey.

You will join the XTM Foundation team as Filigran's internal reference on AI-Native engineering. You'll propose our approach, build our practices, run experiments, and share the results so that teams can change how they work with confidence. You'll be hands-on, opinionated, and always one step ahead.

💼 Your Responsibilities

  • Define and own Filigran's AI-Native engineering strategy: which tools, which workflows, which practices, and how they evolve as the landscape moves fast.

  • Run structured experiments to evaluate new AI coding tools and agents (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Cline, MCP servers, code generation agents…), measure their real impact on velocity and quality, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.

  • Build the guardrails and engineering standards that ensure AI-generated code is maintainable, tested, and consistent with our quality bar — not just fast to produce.

  • Work directly with product engineering teams (~80 engineers) to embed AI practices into their day-to-day workflows: pair programming with AI, AI-assisted code review, test generation, documentation, and beyond.

  • Share what you learn. Run internal talks, workshops, and demos. Be the person engineers come to when they want to understand what's possible, and what isn't. Show real results, including the failures.

  • Stay permanently ahead of the curve — the AI tooling landscape moves weekly. You'll be the one tracking it, filtering the noise, and surfacing what actually matters for a team like ours.

  • Work in the XTM Foundation team to turn AI practices into shared building blocks for every product team: agent workflows in our CI pipelines (dependency updates, flaky test triage, review assistance), shared MCP servers and prompt libraries, versioned AI configuration in the repositories, and written rules on tools and data handling that apply to everyone.

  • Contribute to Filigran's external voice on AI-Native engineering — blog posts, open-source contributions, conference talks — as the opportunity arises.

🤝 Who You'll Work With

  • Reports to: Principal Engineer of XTM Foundation team.

  • Key collaborators: Engineers and Engineering Managers across OpenCTI, OpenAEV, and OpenGRC product teams; VP of Technology; CTO.

  • Working model: You will split your time between XTM Foundation team work (research, experimentation, standards) and direct collaboration with product teams to embed AI practices in real engineering workflows.

🧬 Profile We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience — you are a strong engineer first. You understand what good code looks like, and that's what makes your judgment on AI credible.

ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

This is a senior individual contributor role within our global Revenue organization, spanning the full customer lifecycle from early sales conversations through proof of concept, deployment, renewal, and expansion. You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

In this role you will

  • Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

  • Build our global value strategy. Develop the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, discovery approaches, and playbooks that define how ElevenLabs approaches value across industries and use cases.

  • Scale what works. Turn bespoke work with our largest customers into repeatable approaches that enable our Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial teams to articulate and measure value without requiring bespoke support for every customer.

  • Identify where ElevenLabs can have the greatest impact. Develop a deep understanding of a customer's business, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities to determine which use cases have the greatest potential and why.

  • Quantify the opportunity. Build rigorous financial and operational models that translate ElevenLabs use cases into measurable outcomes across revenue, cost, productivity, customer experience, and other relevant dimensions.

  • Define how value will be proven. Establish success metrics and measurement approaches for proofs of concept and deployments so that customers and ElevenLabs have a shared understanding of what success looks like from the outset.

  • Measure value realization. Partner with customers and internal teams after deployment to understand the impact ElevenLabs is delivering, identify gaps between expected and realized value, and determine where additional opportunities exist.

  • Support expansion and long-term customer value. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.

  • Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.

  • Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.

  • Influence senior stakeholders. Communicate complex analysis simply and credibly, and engage with senior leaders internally and externally when the opportunity requires it.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of relevant experience across operating roles, strategy, management consulting, analytics, finance, customer strategy, or other roles requiring rigorous business problem solving.

  • Strong operating judgment. You understand how businesses work and can quickly get underneath a customer's operating model, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities.

  • Exceptional analytical ability. You can personally build sophisticated financial and operational models, work with incomplete or imperfect information, make assumptions explicit, and turn analysis into decisions.

description:
ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation.

Au sein du Département Automatique, Productique et Informatique, le poste sera associé à l’équipe TASC (Théorie, Algorithmes et Systèmes en Contraintes ) dont les thématiques de recherche s’articulent autour de la programmation par contraintes, de la théorie aux applications en passant par l’hybridation. Dans ce cadre, le poste a pour objectif de venir en soutien au développement du solveur de contraintes choco-solver (http://choco-solver.org) maintenu par l’équipe TASC.

 

MISSIONS

Sous la responsabilité fonctionnelle du responsable du projet et développeur principal de la plateforme Choco-solver et en collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe TASC, les missions principales du poste sont :

  1.   Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur, telles que GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort ou Circuit ;

  2.   Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes (p. ex. le moteur de propagation) ;

  3.   Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (lazy) dans les contraintes Sum et AllDifferent, entre autres ;

  4.   Participer à la rédaction d’articles scientifiques liés à ces sujets.

 

 ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission

 

  1.      Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur

·       Analyse les algorithmes de filtrage de GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort et Circuit disponibles dans choco-solver et identifie les parcours en profondeur (composantes fortement connexes, chemins alternants, etc.) susceptibles de bénéficier de l’approche bimodale

·       Conçoit et implémente en Java les variantes bimodales de ces algorithmes, en garantissant le niveau de cohérence attendu

·     Vérifie la correction des implémentations par des tests unitaires et des tests aléatoires comparant les résultats avec les propagateurs existants

·       Mesure les gains obtenus (temps de filtrage, passage à l’échelle) sur des jeux d’instances de référence (XCSP3, MiniZinc Challenge)

·       Intègre les développements validés dans la version publique de choco-solver (revue de code, documentation, intégration continue)

 

2.      Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes

·       Étudie le fonctionnement interne de choco-solver (moteur de propagation, ordonnancement des propagateurs, gestion des événements) afin d’identifier les mécanismes pouvant tirer parti d’une stratégie bimodale

·       Propose et prototype une ou plusieurs adaptations, par exemple un basculement dynamique entre modes de propagation

·       Évalue expérimentalement ces prototypes et analyse les compromis entre coût et bénéfice

 

3.      Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (

  • Assister en run les équipes de développement sur le projet de transition de plateforme: nous sommes actuellement sous Windows/.NET/.NETCore et nous sommes en train de passer sur Linux/NETCore/NodeJS. Nous souhaitons remplacer notre architecture monolithique par une architecture de microservices

title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
description:
Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école 
 
Thiga en 30 secondes : 

Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris.
Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours
 
Pourquoi ce poste : 

L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite.

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir.


Ce que tu vas faire 🖇

1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events

  • Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription

  • Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas

  • Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée

  • Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA

  • Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com

  • Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister

  • Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence

    • 2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer

    Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires.

  • Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions

  • Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne

  • Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater

  • Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions

    • 3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel

    L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel.

  • Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA

  • Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable

    • L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous, c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel LinkedIn. C'est ce qui te permet d'avancer vite et de tester dix fois plus d'hypothèses qu'une équipe classique.


    La stack que tu vas pratiquer 🧰

    Le growth marketing moderne, c'est une combinaison d'intuition testée par la donnée, de vitesse d'exécution et de bons outils au bon moment.

  • LLM et agents : Claude (Pro et Code), Gemini

  • Génération visuelle et audio : Nano Banana, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, HeyGen

  • Marketing ops : HubSpot (CRM, marketing hub, workflows), Luma, Phantom Buster

  • Prise de notes et capitalisation : Granola, Notion AI

  • Vibe coding (en bonus, pour les profils qui veulent aller plus loin) : Lovable, Cursor pour bricoler des micro-outils internes

    • Tu n'as pas besoin de tout maîtriser à l'arrivée. On attend une vraie curiosité et l'envie de pratiquer, pas un CV exhaustif.


    Le profil que nous recherchons 🌟

  • Formation : école de commerce ou de communication, en M1 ou M2, idéalement avec une spécialisation marketing, growth ou entrepreneuriat

  • Pratique IA personnelle prouvée : tu as un side project, un compte ChatGPT ou Claude que tu utilises tous les jours, un workflow Make ou n8n que tu as construit, un agent custom, un blog assisté par LLM, un repo GitHub, ou n'importe quoi qui démontre que l'IA est dans ta vie.

  • Réflexe growth : tu penses en funnel avant de penser en campagne, tu formules des hypothèses avant de produire, et tester puis mesurer te vient plus naturellement que produire pour produire

  • Appétence data : Excel ou Google Sheets n'ont pas de secret pour toi, et l'idée de creuser un dashboard pour comprendre pourquoi un taux de conversion a bougé t'intéresse plus qu'elle ne t'ennuie

  • Fibre communication : tu sais écrire pour être lu, tu as déjà animé une page, un compte ou une communauté

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer – LLMs
description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

Who we’re looking for

We're seeking a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to train domain-specific language models and provide technical leadership to the team. You'll own critical parts of our training infrastructure, mentor engineers, and drive technical decisions from data preparation through production deployment. You have deep hands-on experience training language models at scale, lead by example through rigorous experimentation and high-quality code, and are motivated by seeing your work deployed to millions of users. You thrive in fast-paced environments where you balance technical depth with practical business impact.

What you’ll do

  • Analyze model performance and training data, formulate hypotheses, design and execute rigorous experiments to systematically improve model quality, training and inference efficiency, and downstream task performance

  • Drive technical decision-making for model architecture, training strategies, and infrastructure choices

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to ML engineers and interns, conducting code reviews, sharing best practices, and accelerating team growth

  • Train large language models through continued pre-training and full parameter fine-tuning on proprietary datasets

  • Build and optimize distributed training infrastructure across multi-node GPU clusters using frameworks like DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron-LM, or Axolotl

  • Own large-scale data preparation: filtering, quality assessment, deduplication, and data mixture strategies for training corpora at 100B+ token scale

  • Generate and curate high-quality synthetic data for instruction fine-tuning and capability enhancement

  • Debug training stability issues, optimize training and inference throughput (quantization, distillation, serving optimization), and monitor model performance throughout long-running distributed jobs

  • Build robust evaluation frameworks and establish metrics to measure model quality and guide decisions

  • Write production-grade, well-tested code and set engineering standards for the team

Minimum qualifications

  • 7+ years of ML engineering experience

  • Technical leadership experience: mentoring engineers, conducting code reviews, making architecture decisions, and delivering projects with measurable business impact

  • Proven experience training and deploying language models to production (embedding models, encoder models, or large language models) including pre-training, continued pre-training, or fine-tuning with rigorous evaluation and inference optimization

  • Experience preparing large-scale training datasets: data filtering, quality assessment, deduplication strategies, and data mixture design

  • Hands-on experience with distributed training frameworks (DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron-LM, or Axolotl) including orchestrating multi-node jobs, debugging failures, and optimizing throughput

  • Strong understanding of training dynamics at scale: debugging loss instabilities, tuning learning rate schedules, managing training stability across long-running multi-node jobs

  • Expert Python and PyTorch with production experience using training libraries (Transformers, DeepSpeed, Accelerate)

Preferred qualifications

  • Published research at ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), released models on Hugging Face, created public benchmarks, or contributed to open-source projects

  • Experience with post-training methods: RLHF, DPO, GRPO, or other reinforcement learning approaches for alignment and instruction-following

  • Experience optimizing models for production inference including quantization, model compression, distillation, and serving frameworks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM)

  • Understanding of memory optimization: gradient checkpointing, mixed precision training (FP16, BF16, FP8), ZeRO optimization

  • Deep knowledge of GPU architectures (A100, H100, H200) and their implications for training and inference optimization

  • Track record of building synthetic data generation pipelines for instruction tuning or domain adaptation

What we offer

  • High-impact AI projects that are strategically vital to the company, with direct engagement from senior leadership including the CEO

  • State-of-the-art infrastructure: H200 GPU fleet, massive proprietary datasets, access to frontier models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Together.ai) for evaluation and baselines

  • Expert colleagues who have released top Hugging Face models, authored papers at NeurIPS, created well-known benchmarks, and built multiple production AI systems

  • Significant autonomy and freedom to test ideas, experiment with new approaches, and drive technical decisions

  • Modern tooling: Latest ML frameworks, coding assistants, best-in-class development environment

  • Hybrid work model with our Amsterdam office - home to the AI House, bringing together 200+ AI professionals through events, meetups, and startup collaborations

  •  Competitive compensation, top-spec MacBook Pro, and an environment genuinely built for professional growth and learning

  • If you're excited to apply your LLM training expertise to high-impact applications at scale, lead technical initiatives, and grow the next generation of ML engineers, let's talk.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.
